title: Phase 4a follow-up (2 of 2): PSBT parity through the curve capability: xpub point, partial-sig DER, x-only keys, control-block key
description:
## Outcome
`packages/bitcoin`'s PSBT field decoder rejects every v0 PSBT that rust-bitcoin 0.32.8 rejects
because a key or signature fails libsecp256k1's own parse, on the four rules below, through the
supplied curve capability, so the port exits non-zero wherever cyberkrill does on them (plan §3):

1. **Global xpub embedded point.** Key-data bytes 45-77 must be a valid 33-byte compressed point:
   `Xpub::decode` calls `secp256k1::PublicKey::from_slice` (`src/bip32.rs:789-815`). The existing
   strict `isValidPubkey` on those 33 bytes is exactly this rule.
2. **Partial-signature DER.** The value without its last (sighash) byte must be non-empty and pass
   `secp256k1_ecdsa_signature_parse_der` (`src/crypto/ecdsa.rs:38-43`; secp256k1 0.29.1
   `Signature::from_der`, `src/ecdsa/mod.rs:52-71`).
3. **X-only keys on the curve.** `XOnlyPublicKey::from_slice` is `secp256k1_xonly_pubkey_parse`
   (secp256k1 0.29.1 `src/key.rs:1162-1180`; rust-bitcoin `src/psbt/serialize.rs:263-266,295-301`). It applies to
   `PSBT_IN_TAP_INTERNAL_KEY` and `PSBT_OUT_TAP_INTERNAL_KEY` values, and to the x-only part of
   `PSBT_IN_TAP_BIP32_DERIVATION`, `PSBT_OUT_TAP_BIP32_DERIVATION` and `PSBT_IN_TAP_SCRIPT_SIG` keys.
4. **Control-block internal key.** Bytes 1-32 of a `PSBT_IN_TAP_LEAF_SCRIPT` key's control block take
   the same x-only parse (`src/taproot/mod.rs:1117-1118`).

## Why this exists
The rest of the parity gaps Phase 4a (1 of 3)'s README "Deltas not taken" lists; `lck-phase-4a-psbt-field-parity-6yo` fixes the
ones that need no curve operation. Phase 7c's goldens depend on both.

## How the curve checks reach pure code
`bitcoin` never imports `secp256k1` (AGENTS.md package boundaries), so:
- `PubkeyCapability` gains two operations, `isValidXOnlyPubkey : ByteArray → Bool` (32 bytes,
  `secp256k1_xonly_pubkey_parse`) and `isValidDerSignature : ByteArray → Bool`
  (`secp256k1_ecdsa_signature_parse_der`, false on empty input). Rule 1 reuses `isValidPubkey`.
- `secp256k1` adds the two functions with C shims beside the existing ones, each tested on
  published vectors under the third-party rule (for example BIP340's public keys, including its
  off-curve one, and Wycheproof DER cases read at test time as `compressPubkey`'s tests read theirs)
  and on the off-curve x and DER edits below.
- The decoder calls `cap.isValidXOnlyPubkey` and `cap.isValidDerSignature`. The test capability in
  `BitcoinTests/Psbt.lean` stays a shape-only stand-in that rejects exactly the synthetic encodings
  below, so `bitcoin`'s tests prove the routing and the `secp256k1` tests prove the operations. If Phase 7a has already wired the real capability into the
  app, extend that wiring with the two operations.
- Raw bytes are still kept, so the round-trip theorem's shape is unchanged; adding fields to the
  capability changes no theorem statement (they are all for every `cap`).

## Must-reject vectors
Each vector is one published valid v0 vector with exactly one record changed. The off-curve x is
`00…05` (32 bytes, x = 5): 5³ + 7 = 132 is a quadratic non-residue mod p, so no point has it. All
were checked on 2026-10-22 with a throwaway cargo probe pinned to cyberkrill @ 27cad1f's
`Cargo.lock` (bitcoin 0.32.8, secp256k1 0.29.1) calling `Psbt::deserialize`, which returned the
error shown; the port at Phase 4a (1 of 3) accepts every one. That probe is not in the
repository; Scope says how this bead confirms the results reproducibly.

| Vector | Base vector | One-record edit | rust-bitcoin 0.32.8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xpub-point` | BIP174 "PSBT with `PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB`." | first `PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB` key: keep the point's prefix byte, replace its 32 x bytes with the off-curve x | `XPubKey("Can't deserialize ExtendedPublicKey from global XPUB key data")` |
| `partial-sig-der` | BIP174 "PSBT with one P2SH-P2WSH input of a 2-of-2 multisig, redeemScript, witnessScript, and keypaths are available. Contains one signature." | input 0 `PSBT_IN_PARTIAL_SIG` value: first byte `30` becomes `31` | `InvalidEcdsaSignature(Secp256k1(InvalidSignature))` |
| `partial-sig-no-der` | the same | that value becomes the single byte `01` | `InvalidEcdsaSignature(Secp256k1(InvalidSignature))` |
| `xonly-in-internal` | BIP371 "PSBT with one P2TR key only input with internal key, its derivation path, and signature" | input 0 `PSBT_IN_TAP_INTERNAL_KEY` value becomes the off-curve x | `InvalidXOnlyPublicKey` |
| `xonly-in-tap-bip32` | the same | input 0 `PSBT_IN_TAP_BIP32_DERIVATION` key data becomes the off-curve x | `InvalidXOnlyPublicKey` |
| `xonly-in-tap-script-sig` | BIP371 "PSBT with one P2TR script path only input with dummy internal key, scripts, script key derivation paths, merkle root, and script path signatures" | input 0 first `PSBT_IN_TAP_SCRIPT_SIG` key: its x-only part becomes the off-curve x | `InvalidXOnlyPublicKey` |
| `xonly-out-internal` | BIP371 "PSBT with one P2TR key only output with internal key and its derivation path" | output 0 `PSBT_OUT_TAP_INTERNAL_KEY` value becomes the off-curve x | `InvalidXOnlyPublicKey` |
| `xonly-out-tap-bip32` | the same | output 0 `PSBT_OUT_TAP_BIP32_DERIVATION` key data becomes the off-curve x | `InvalidXOnlyPublicKey` |
| `control-block-internal` | the script-path input vector above | input 0 first `PSBT_IN_TAP_LEAF_SCRIPT` key: control-block bytes 1-32 become the off-curve x | `InvalidControlBlock` |

Must-accept: the five unchanged bases, which both accept today.

## Scope
- The two capability operations, their `secp256k1` C shims and tests, and the decoder calls.
- A committed script derives every vector above from the pinned published vectors (the same script
  as `lck-phase-4a-psbt-field-parity-6yo`'s, extended). Tests assert each vector fails with a named reason under the test
  capability.
- One production-mutation red run per rule and per field (five x-only sites count as five), and one
  per new `secp256k1` function, recorded like the existing runners.
- Update `check-tx-psbt-copy.py`, `docs/upstream-fixes.md` and README as in `lck-phase-4a-psbt-field-parity-6yo`; README "Deltas
  not taken" then lists no PSBT parity row: the three port-stricter rules are taken deltas
  (owner decision 2026-10-23, `lck-decide-psbt-port-stricter-mnx`), which `lck-phase-4a-psbt-field-parity-6yo` lists under
  "Deltas taken".
- The expected results above come from an uncommitted probe and are provisional: confirm each
  vector's exit with the committed reference capture exactly as `lck-phase-4a-psbt-field-parity-6yo` describes (its script
  extended), with the same hand-derived fallback and the same rule for a vector that differs.

## Non-goals
- Signature verification, sighash computation, signing.
- Anything `lck-phase-4a-psbt-field-parity-6yo` owns, including the port-stricter rules it documents and tests
  (owner decision 2026-10-23, `lck-decide-psbt-port-stricter-mnx`).

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- Phase 4a (3 of 3)'s theorems keep their statements (every change is in `decode`, which `valid`
  assumes succeeds). If a proof breaks, repair it; never weaken a statement; otherwise follow the
  common stop mechanics.
- C stays only in `secp256k1`; the one-OpenSSL check still passes.

## Dependencies / ordering
- Depends on `lck-phase-4a-psbt-field-parity-6yo` (both edit `Fields.lean`; one at a time).
- Phase 7c depends on this bead and adds every must-reject vector here to its exit-status goldens
  (both exit non-zero).

## Acceptance Criteria
- All nine must-reject vectors are rejected with named reasons; the unchanged bases parse.
- `Secp256k1.isValidXOnlyPubkey` and `Secp256k1.isValidDerSignature` exist with vector tests.
- One production mutation per rule, site and new function fails its test, recorded.
- Phase 4a (3 of 3)'s theorems unchanged and `#print axioms` clean; `nix flake check` passes.
- A committed capture script and its output confirm every expected exit against the pinned
  cyberkrill build, or README marks an expectation hand-derived as AGENTS.md allows.
close_reason: PSBT field decoding now matches rust-bitcoin 0.32.8 on four curve rules through two new PubkeyCapability operations (isValidXOnlyPubkey, isValidDerSignature) and their secp256k1 shims: global xpub point (isValidPubkey on bytes 45-77), partial-signature DER, five x-only sites (input/output internal keys, input/output tap BIP32 keys, tap script-sig keys) and the control-block internal key. All nine must-reject vectors fail with named reasons and the six bases parse. Offline capture of the pinned cyberkrill 27cad1f: 49 rows (19 must-reject, 14 must-accept, 16 port-stricter); the original 39 are unchanged, the nine new rejections exit 1 with the expected rust-bitcoin error text, and the new key-only-output base exits 0; no expectation is hand-derived. Vectors: BIP340 public keys 19 rows, 17 parsed, indices 5 and 14 rejected, plus lengths 0/31/33 and x = 5; Wycheproof DER measured 476 cases, 168 valid parsed, 162 encoding-flagged rejected, ModifiedSignature 31 rejected and 17 parsed. Red runs: eight PSBT site mutations (PSBT mutations 125/125) and one per new function (secp256k1 negative mutations 44/44, compression 18/18); the other runners report 6/6, 6/6, 18/18, 20/20 and 8/8. Theorem statements are unchanged; the axiom gate reports 764 library theorems, 60 named, 0 offenders; PSBT checks 101/101. Both packages' lake build and lake test, nix flake check and nix build exit 0.

title: Phase 4a follow-up (1 of 2): PSBT field parity with rust-bitcoin 0.32.8: xpub version, sighash bytes, leaf versions, proprietary key length
description:
## Outcome
`packages/bitcoin`'s PSBT field decoder rejects every v0 PSBT that rust-bitcoin 0.32.8 rejects on the
five rules below, none of which needs a curve operation, and still accepts every PSBT it accepts
today that rust-bitcoin 0.32.8 also accepts. cyberkrill's `onchain-decode-psbt` parses with
`Psbt::from_str` (`main.rs:2329`), that is Base64 then `Psbt::deserialize`, so the port then exits
non-zero wherever cyberkrill does on these rules (plan §3).

1. **Global xpub version bytes.** The 78-byte key data must start with `0488b21e` (xpub) or
   `043587cf` (tpub): `Xpub::decode`, `src/bip32.rs:789-801`, called from
   `src/psbt/map/global.rs:113-118`.
2. **Partial-signature sighash byte.** A `PSBT_IN_PARTIAL_SIG` value is a DER signature plus one
   sighash byte, which must be a standard ECDSA type: `01`, `02`, `03`, `81`, `82` or `83`; an empty
   value is rejected (`src/crypto/ecdsa.rs:38-43`, `src/psbt/serialize.rs:179-200`). The DER part is
   `lck-phase-4a-psbt-curve-parity-5sk`'s.
3. **Taproot signature sighash byte.** A 65-byte `PSBT_IN_TAP_KEY_SIG` or `PSBT_IN_TAP_SCRIPT_SIG`
   value must end in `00`, `01`, `02`, `03`, `81`, `82` or `83` (`src/crypto/taproot.rs:30-44`,
   `src/crypto/sighash.rs:500-512`). The 64-byte form is unchanged.
4. **Leaf versions.** `LeafVersion::from_consensus` rejects odd values and the annex byte `0x50`
   (`src/taproot/mod.rs:1236-1243`). It applies to the last byte of a `PSBT_IN_TAP_LEAF_SCRIPT` value
   (`src/psbt/serialize.rs:326-336`), to the first control-block byte masked with `0xfe`
   (`src/taproot/mod.rs:1116`), and to every `PSBT_OUT_TAP_TREE` leaf
   (`src/psbt/serialize.rs:380-396`). Today the port checks only evenness, and only in output trees.
5. **Proprietary key length.** After the identifier and the subtype, a proprietary key carries at
   most 1,024 bytes (`src/psbt/raw.rs:158-173`; the whole-key decode at `:193-199` rejects what is
   left over). This one is not in README's original "Deltas not taken" table; the vector check below
   found it.

## Why this exists
Phase 4a (1 of 3) copied lean-miniscript's field rules unchanged outside the capability and
preimage routing, and its README "Deltas not taken" lists where they accept PSBTs that rust-bitcoin
0.32.8 rejects. Plan §3 requires exit parity with cyberkrill except for its four documented
deltas, so these are fixed rather than documented. Phase 7c's `onchain-decode-psbt` goldens depend
on it.

## Must-reject vectors
Each vector is one published valid v0 vector with exactly one record changed. All were checked on
2026-10-22 with a throwaway cargo probe pinned to cyberkrill @ 27cad1f's `Cargo.lock` (bitcoin
0.32.8, secp256k1 0.29.1) calling `Psbt::deserialize`, which returned the error shown. The port at
Phase 4a (1 of 3) (`Psbt.parse` with the test capability) accepts every one. That probe is not in
the repository; Scope says how this bead confirms the results reproducibly.

| Vector | Base vector | One-record edit | rust-bitcoin 0.32.8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xpub-version` | BIP174 "PSBT with `PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB`." | first `PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB` key: key-data bytes 0-3 become `04b24746` (the SLIP-132 zpub version) | `XPubKey("Can't deserialize ExtendedPublicKey from global XPUB key data")` |
| `partial-sig-sighash` | BIP174 "PSBT with one P2SH-P2WSH input of a 2-of-2 multisig, redeemScript, witnessScript, and keypaths are available. Contains one signature." (below: "the one-signature vector") | input 0 `PSBT_IN_PARTIAL_SIG` value: last byte becomes `04` | `NonStandardSighashType(4)` |
| `partial-sig-empty` | the one-signature vector | input 0 `PSBT_IN_PARTIAL_SIG` value becomes empty | `InvalidEcdsaSignature(EmptySignature)` |
| `tap-key-sig-sighash` | BIP371 "PSBT with one P2TR key only input with internal key, its derivation path, and signature" | input 0 `PSBT_IN_TAP_KEY_SIG` value: its 64 bytes plus `04` | `NonStandardSighashType(4)` |
| `tap-script-sig-sighash` | BIP371 "PSBT with one P2TR script path only input with dummy internal key, scripts, script key derivation paths, merkle root, and script path signatures" (below: "the script-path input vector") | input 0 first `PSBT_IN_TAP_SCRIPT_SIG` value: its first 64 bytes plus `04` | `NonStandardSighashType(4)` |
| `leaf-script-odd` | the script-path input vector | input 0 first `PSBT_IN_TAP_LEAF_SCRIPT` value: last byte becomes `c1` | `InvalidLeafVersion` |
| `leaf-script-annex` | the script-path input vector | the same value: last byte becomes `50` | `InvalidLeafVersion` |
| `control-block-annex` | the script-path input vector | that record's key: control-block byte 0 becomes `50` OR its old parity bit | `InvalidControlBlock` |
| `out-tap-tree-annex` | BIP371 "PSBT with one P2TR script path only output with dummy internal key, taproot tree, and script key derivation paths" | output 0 `PSBT_OUT_TAP_TREE` value: the first leaf's version byte becomes `50` | `InvalidLeafVersion` |
| `proprietary-1025` | the one-signature vector | input 0 gains a record with key `fc 01 41 00` followed by 1,025 zero bytes, value `00` | `ConsensusEncoding(ParseFailed("data not consumed entirely when explicitly deserializing"))` |

Must-accept boundaries, all accepted by both today: the five unchanged bases above; the
one-signature vector with sighash `83`; the key-sig vector with a 65th byte of `00` and of `83`;
leaf-script and output-tree leaf version `c2`; control-block byte 0 `c2` OR parity; the xpub vector
with version `043587cf`; `proprietary-1025` with 1,024 zero bytes instead.

## Scope
- Tighten the field rules in `Bitcoin/Psbt/Fields.lean` (decode only; framing in `Codec.lean` does
  not change), each failing with a named `invalidKey`/`invalidValue` reason.
- A committed script derives every vector above from the pinned published vectors, by base name and
  edit, under the third-party rule. Tests assert each must-reject vector fails with its named reason
  and each must-accept boundary still parses.
- One production-mutation red run per rule and per field the rule covers (the three leaf-version sites
  count as three), recorded like `check-psbt-mutations.py`.
- Update `check-tx-psbt-copy.py`'s documented edits and `docs/upstream-fixes.md` for each change to
  copied code, and README: move each fixed row out of "Deltas not taken".
- The expected results above come from an uncommitted probe, so they are provisional until this
  bead confirms them with AGENTS.md's reference rule: run `onchain-decode-psbt` from the pinned
  cyberkrill build (`nix build --no-link github:douglaz/cyberkrill/27cad1faba86260b06665a89f0af5134d23525c2`)
  on each vector's Base64 text, and commit the capture script and its output (exit status and
  streams per vector). If neither that build nor a throwaway clone of that commit builds, cite the
  rust-bitcoin 0.32.8 rule for each vector and mark the expectation hand-derived in README, as
  AGENTS.md says; never fall back to the uncommitted probe. A vector whose confirmed exit differs
  from the table is not implemented as written: record it and leave that rule unchanged.

## Port-stricter rules kept (owner decision, 2026-10-23)
`lck-decide-psbt-port-stricter-mnx` closed with all three BIP rules kept, after two independent
reviews picked "keep" 2-0 on each: key types and proprietary subtypes are canonical CompactSize
(BIP174), the global xpub path length must match the key's depth (BIP174), and a v0 PSBT may not
carry v2-only fields (BIP370). Their code does not change. On 16 inputs cyberkrill is expected to
exit 0 and the port to exit non-zero (the capture below decides), which makes them a documented,
tested exception to golden parity once captured and tested (plan §3 counts it as the fourth).
This bead documents and tests them:
- **Capture.** The committed capture script in Scope also runs the pinned cyberkrill build's
  `onchain-decode-psbt` on the 16 inputs: the three key-type vectors and the xpub-depth vector below
  (derived by the same script from their published bases), and BIP370 invalid vectors 1-12
  ("PSBTv0 but with PSBT_GLOBAL_TX_VERSION." through "PSBTv0 but with PSBT_OUT_SCRIPT."). The
  expected zero exits so far come only from `Psbt::deserialize` in an uncommitted probe, so they are
  provisional until this capture confirms them.
- **Rejection tests** for the four inputs not yet pinned, each asserting its named reason. The
  first three add one input-0 record with value `00` to the one-signature vector:
  - `key-type-fd01`: key `fd 01`, failing with `decode truncated`;
  - `key-type-fd0500`: key `fd 05 00`, failing with `nonCanonicalCompactSize`;
  - `proprietary-subtype-fd01`: proprietary key `fc 01 41 fd 01`, failing with
    `invalidKey "input" 252 "malformed proprietary key"`;
  - `xpub-depth`: BIP174 "PSBT with `PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB`." with the first xpub key's depth byte
    (key-data byte 4) XOR 1, failing with
    `invalidValue "global" 1 "path length must match the extended key depth"`.

  The twelve BIP370 vectors are already pinned as must-reject; keep them pinned.
- **README.** List the three rules and the 16 inputs, with each input's captured cyberkrill exit,
  under "Deltas taken". Remove the key-type row from Phase 4a (1 of 3)'s "Deltas not taken".
- **plan §3.** Add the entry for this exception beside "BIP370 v2 PSBTs". The count there already
  says "a fourth".
- If the capture shows cyberkrill exiting non-zero on any of the 16, that input is ordinary exit
  parity: record it, keep its port test, and leave it out of the delta.

## Non-goals
- Checks that need a curve operation (xpub point, DER, x-only keys, control-block internal key):
  `lck-phase-4a-psbt-curve-parity-5sk`.
- Changing the port-stricter rules (CompactSize key types, xpub depth/path, v0 PSBTs with v2-only
  fields): the owner kept all three (owner decision 2026-10-23, `lck-decide-psbt-port-stricter-mnx`), so their code stays as it
  is; this bead only captures, tests and documents them ("Port-stricter rules kept").
- BIP370 v2 rules; roles; signing.

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- Phase 4a (3 of 3)'s theorems keep their statements. Every change here is in `decode`, which `valid`
  already assumes succeeds, so tightening only shrinks `valid`. If a proof unfolds a changed rule and
  breaks, repair the proof; never weaken a statement. If that is out of reach, follow the common stop
  mechanics.
- Every pinned published valid vector still parses and every pinned invalid vector is still
  rejected.

## Dependencies / ordering
- Depends on Phase 4a (3 of 3), so its proofs land first.
- `lck-phase-4a-psbt-curve-parity-5sk` and Phase 7c depend on this bead. Phase 7c adds every must-reject
  vector here to its exit-status goldens (both exit non-zero).

## Acceptance Criteria
- All ten must-reject vectors are rejected with named reasons, and all must-accept boundaries parse.
- One production mutation per rule and site fails its test, recorded.
- Phase 4a (3 of 3)'s theorems unchanged and `#print axioms` clean; `nix flake check` passes.
- A committed capture script and its output confirm every expected exit against the pinned
  cyberkrill build, or README marks an expectation hand-derived as AGENTS.md allows. This
  includes the 16 port-stricter inputs.
- The four new port-stricter rejection tests pass with their named reasons, and the twelve
  BIP370 must-reject vectors stay pinned.
- README "Deltas taken" and plan §3 carry the port-stricter entry, and the key-type row has
  left Phase 4a (1 of 3)'s "Deltas not taken".
close_reason: Done. Five non-curve PSBT decode rules in packages/bitcoin Bitcoin/Psbt/Fields.lean now match rust-bitcoin 0.32.8, each failing with a named invalidKey/invalidValue reason: global xpub version 0488b21e or 043587cf; partial-signature value nonempty and ending in a standard ECDSA sighash byte (01/02/03/81/82/83); 65-byte Taproot key and script signatures ending in 00/01/02/03/81/82/83; leaf versions even and not 0x50 at the leaf-script value, the control-block byte masked with 0xfe and every output-tree leaf; proprietary keys at most 1,024 bytes after rust-bitcoin's one-byte subtype, in all three maps. Framing, serializers and the three kept BIP rules are unchanged. capture-cyberkrill-psbt.py runs the pinned cyberkrill 27cad1f onchain-decode-psbt offline on 39 inputs derived from the published BIP174/370/371 vectors; test-data/cyberkrill-psbt-capture.json records 39 rows: 10 must-reject (all exit 1, stderr naming the expected rust-bitcoin error), 13 must-accept (all exit 0) and 16 port-stricter (all exit 0 upstream and rejected by the port; the fourth documented golden-parity exception in plan section 3 and README Deltas taken). Tests: 39 new PSBT actions (91/91), exact reasons for the 10 rejections and the 4 new port-stricter tests (decode truncated, decode nonCanonicalCompactSize, malformed proprietary key, path length must match the extended key depth), all 13 acceptances; the 12 BIP370 must-reject vectors stay pinned. Red runs: 22 new production mutations recorded in psbt-mutations.json (95 to 117 records); the six mutation runners detect 6/6, 6/6, 18/18, 20/20, 117/117 and 8/8 (175). Axiom gate: 764 library theorems, 60 named, 0 offenders; no theorem statement changed. Copied-code edits registered in check-tx-psbt-copy.py (10/10 against a fresh lean-miniscript cb9bc5f checkout) and docs/upstream-fixes.md. lake build, lake test, nix flake check -L and nix build exit 0.

title: Phase 4a (3 of 3): PSBT and transaction proofs: serialize/parse round-trips, duplicate-key and trailing-data rejection
description:
## Outcome
`packages/bitcoin` proves, over the code Phase 4a (1 of 3) ported:
- `parse cap hashes (serialize p) = .ok p` for every PSBT `p` with `valid cap hashes p`, where `valid` is defined explicitly without `parse` or `serialize`;
- the PSBT parser rejects duplicate keys and trailing data;
- the transaction codec round-trips for transactions the wire format can carry (`Transaction.WellFormed`).

## Why this exists
Plan §2 lists the first two as `bitcoin`'s PSBT obligations. Its "CompactSize and serialization: round-trip" obligation covers transactions too, and no other bead owns that one.

## Scope
- **Copy** `LeanMiniscript/Psbt/CodecProofs.lean` and `Psbt/ParseProofs.lean` from lean-miniscript @ `cb9bc5f`, and port them. Build on them rather than reproving:
  - `Psbt.parse_serialize` (`ParseProofs.lean:31-34`) takes **two** hypotheses, `formed : psbt.WellFormed` and `decodes : psbt.decode = .ok decoded`, and concludes `Psbt.parse psbt.serialize = .ok psbt`. `Psbt.parse` is framing plus `psbt.decode`'s field validation (`Fields.lean:536-539`), and `decode` is where `validPublicKey` and `preimageHash` run (`Fields.lean:206-207`, `:272-276`). After Phase 4a (1 of 3), `parse` and `decode` take the pubkey capability `cap` and the preimage-hash parameter `hashes`.
  - `Psbt.serialize_parse` (`:40`): accepted bytes are `serialize` of a PSBT that is `WellFormed` and decodes.
- **Define `valid`** explicitly: `valid cap hashes p := p.WellFormed ∧ ∃ d, p.decode cap hashes = .ok d`. It may use the field decoder, never `parse` or `serialize`, and it matches `parse_serialize`'s two hypotheses. `WellFormed` alone is not enough: the round-trip is false for a PSBT with a key the capability rejects.
- Derive the duplicate-key and trailing-data rejections from `Psbt.serialize_parse` and `KeyValueMap.WellFormed`, which includes `Unique` (`Codec.lean:68-69`).
- Show that `valid` holds on every valid vector, using Phase 4a (1 of 3)'s test capability and stand-in hashes. No valid vector carries a RIPEMD160 or HASH160 field, so Phase 4a (2 of 3) is not needed for that.
- **The statements** (upstream has no transaction round-trip: `DeserializationProofs.lean` stops at CompactSize, byte vectors and witness stacks):
  - (a) `Psbt.parse cap hashes bytes = .ok p → p.global.Unique ∧ (∀ m ∈ p.inputs, m.Unique) ∧ ∀ m ∈ p.outputs, m.Unique` (from `serialize_parse` and `KeyValueMap.WellFormed`);
  - (b) `Psbt.parse cap hashes bytes = .ok p → Psbt.parse cap hashes (bytes ++ extra) = .ok q → extra = ByteArray.empty` (`Codec.lean:127` throws `.trailingData`);
  - (c) for `tx` with every `txid.size = 32`, every script and witness item size `< 2^64`, `tx.inputs.size < 2^64`, `tx.outputs.size < 2^64`, every witness stack's length `< 2^64`, `witnesses.length = tx.inputs.size`, and `tx.inputs.size > 0 ∨ tx.outputs.size = 0` (a 0-input, 0-output transaction round-trips through the zero-flag path, `Deserialization.lean:120-123`): `parseTransaction (serializeWitnessTransaction tx witnesses) = .ok ⟨tx, witnesses'⟩`, where `witnesses' = witnesses` if some stack is non-empty and `tx.inputs.toList.map (fun _ => [])` otherwise.
  - State (c)'s hypotheses as a named `Transaction.WellFormed`. They are inherent to the wire format, not a weakening, and README lists them. The size and count bounds are there because CompactSize carries at most 2^64 − 1 (upstream's `readCompactSize_compactSize` takes `value < 2 ^ 64`, `DeserializationProofs.lean:31`): an `Array` of 2^64 outputs serializes its count as `ff 00…00`, which `readCompactSize` rejects as non-canonical. The unconditional form is false: `readTransaction (allowWitness := true)` reads an empty input vector as the BIP144 marker (`Deserialization.lean:115-147`), `readOutPoint` takes exactly 32 bytes while `txid` is a `ByteArray`, and `serializeWitnessTransaction` treats missing stacks as empty and emits the legacy form when all are empty (`:159-170`).

## Non-goals
- New parser features. RIPEMD-160 and HASH160 (Phase 4a, 2 of 3).
- PSBT role modules.

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- **Never weaken a stated obligation.** If one is out of reach, follow the common stop mechanics.
- Copied files get the common provenance comment (upstream files carry no per-file header); lean-miniscript's MIT notice sits beside them.

## Dependencies / ordering
- Depends on Phase 4a (1 of 3).
- Phase 7a and Phase 8a wait for all three Phase 4a beads.

## Acceptance Criteria
Theorems, with `#print axioms`:
- `∀ cap hashes p, valid cap hashes p → parse cap hashes (serialize p) = .ok p`;
- the parser rejects duplicate keys: statement (a) above;
- the parser rejects trailing data: statement (b) above;
- the transaction serialization round-trip under `Transaction.WellFormed`: statement (c) above.

Tests: `valid` holds on every valid BIP174, BIP370 and BIP371 vector: 34 (BIP174 10, BIP174 signer-failure PSBTs 4, BIP370 14, BIP371 6).
### Common definition of done (plan §4, every work session)
- `nix build` and `nix flake check` exit 0. The flake check runs `lake build && lake test` for every package listed in `lakePackages` in `flake.nix`, inside the nix sandbox, then runs the app. Stage new files (`git add`) before running `nix flake check`: a flake sees only tracked files.
- In each touched package, `nix develop -c lake build` and `nix develop -c lake test` exit 0.
- No `sorry`: `grep -rnw sorry --include='*.lean' --exclude-dir=.lake packages` prints nothing (CI runs the same check from Phase 2 on).
- `#print axioms` on every theorem this bead lists shows only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. Each listed theorem is added to the package's committed axiom-gate test (Phase 2's pattern); `lake test` fails on any axiom outside the three. The gate is an allowlist of those three and contains no "sorry" substring. No `native_decide` in library or proof modules; test files may use it.
- The vector counts this bead states pass. Each test asserts that the number of vectors it loaded equals a pinned constant, so a dropped vector fails, and the test output prints each count (for example `<set> valid: N/N`).
- `README.md` is updated: what the package now provides, vector sources and counts, and anything this bead says to document.
- `AGENTS.md` rules hold, including "Reference only" for any value taken from cyberkrill. New Lean, C and script files we write carry the dual-licence header; third-party and copied files follow the rule below, and JSON and other formats without comments need none.
- **Safety.** Tests use only published vectors, published test mnemonics, the BOLT #11 specification's published example private key (tests only), recordings from a throwaway regtest node, and synthetic or script-generated fixtures under the third-party rule (for example cyberkrill's captured outputs on those inputs, synthetic provider responses, our own LNURL and LUD JSON, values a committed script derives from published inputs). Never anything from the owner's node, wallets or devices. Tests never reach the internet, port 8332 or `~/.bitcoin`. Nothing committed contains private keys, seeds, xprvs, tprvs or WIF keys, or real addresses, xpubs or device dumps, apart from that BOLT #11 example key. No hardware wallets, no signing outside test vectors, no broadcast, no mainnet funds.
- **Third-party material** (`AGENTS.md` "Licence", plan §5):
  - Admitted in the tree, each with a provenance sidecar or header line (source URL, commit, path, licence), never the dual-licence header: MIT, BSD, ISC, CC0 or public domain, and CC-BY-4.0 (attribution and a note of any changes, for example "extracted and reformatted", kept in the sidecar). Material offered under a choice that includes MIT (such as fedimint-lite's `MIT OR Apache-2.0`) is taken under MIT.
  - Kept out of the tree: Apache-2.0-only, share-alike (CC-BY-SA) and unlicensed material. Use a pinned non-flake input read at test time, or replace it with vectors we generate ourselves.
  - Copied code whose upstream file has no header gets a provenance comment (upstream repo, commit, path, "MIT") with the upstream MIT notice in a file beside it, never the dual-licence header.
  - In a Lean file the provenance line is the first line and a `--` line comment (or `/- … -/`), never a `/-! … -/` doc comment, for example `-- Copied from <repo> @ <commit>, <path>; MIT, see <notice file>`. JSON and other formats without comments get the sidecar.
- **Stop mechanics.** If this bead says stop and report: commit no weakened statement, `br defer` the bead, add label `owner-decision`, comment what was tried (`br comments add`), and end the work session blocked.
- **Follow-ups.** A delta or stricter check you think v1 needs goes in a new bead created deferred with label `owner-decision`, and in README "Deltas not taken". Never implement it unranked.

Axiom gate: 764 library theorems, 60 named (56 plus the four), 0 offenders; print axioms on each shows only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Tests: valid holds on 34/34 valid vectors (BIP174 10, signer failures 4, BIP370 14, BIP371 6), each count pinned and printed; Transaction.WellFormed holds on 135/136 embedded transactions, the pinned exception being bip174Valid[9] (0 inputs, 2 outputs), which fails only the inputs-or-no-outputs hypothesis and on which the witness-allowing reader returns the measured DecodeError.truncated. Owner decision (2026-10-19), which closed the RIPEMD-160 question bead: write our own RIPEMD-160 in `bitcoin`, under the repo's MIT OR Apache-2.0 header.

- `febyeji/lean-hash160` is **not** copied. It is Apache-2.0 only, which would make `bitcoin` and every package above it "(MIT OR Apache-2.0) AND Apache-2.0", against plan §5 and §6 #7.
- Skipping the check would break parity: rust-bitcoin 0.32.8, which cyberkrill uses, rejects bad RIPEMD160 and HASH160 preimages.

- `ripemd160 : ByteArray → ByteArray` (20 bytes), written from the algorithm's published description, and `hash160 b = ripemd160 (sha256 b)`.

- A proof that the implementation matches the specification. There is no RIPEMD-160 obligation at level M.

title: Phase 4a (1 of 3): tx and PSBT codec subset copied from lean-miniscript and ported to 4.35, with the pubkey capability and the BIP174/370/371 vectors
description:
## Outcome
`packages/bitcoin` can:
- parse and serialize transactions;
- parse and serialize PSBTs (BIP174 v0, BIP370 v2, BIP371 taproot fields).

The code is a narrow subset copied from `febyeji/lean-miniscript` @ `cb9bc5f` (written for v4.32.0, MIT), ported to v4.35.0 and owned by this repo from then on. The public-key validity check that upstream did through its own `ECDSA.parsePublicKey` becomes a **supplied capability** with two checks: the strict rule for `partial_sigs` keys and libsecp256k1's own rule for `bip32_derivation` keys (owner decision 2026-10-21, `lck-decide-hybrid-pubkey-xgr`). The RIPEMD160 and HASH160 preimage checks sit behind a parameter, which Phase 4a (2 of 3) fills. The BIP174/370/371 vectors pass.

## Why this exists
`onchain-decode-psbt` (Phase 7c) parses PSBTs. The Core RPC commands (Phase 8) receive PSBTs from `createpsbt` and `walletcreatefundedpsbt` and decode them.

Owner decision P3 (2026-10-19): copy rather than rewrite, take the narrow subset, add our own level-M proofs, and send general fixes upstream. Phase 4a is split in three to keep each work session small: this port, then our own RIPEMD-160 and HASH160 (2 of 3), then the new proofs (3 of 3).

## Scope
- **Copy** `LeanMiniscript/Psbt/Codec.lean`, `LeanMiniscript/Psbt/Fields.lean` and their dependencies:
  - transaction types and codec;
  - `Bitcoin/Serialization.lean`, `Bitcoin/Deserialization.lean`, `Bitcoin/DeserializationProofs.lean`. Phase 3a (1 of 4) already copied `Serialization.lean` whole and slices of the other two (`Deserialization.lean` L11-79, `DeserializationProofs.lean` L7-179) into one module, unless its README records why it wrote its own: import that module and copy only the remaining lines (tx readers, `txid`, witness serialization), with provenance comments naming the line ranges;
  - the script syntax they need;
  - `Bitcoin/Base64.lean`.
  - About 1,400 lines, plus their tests and the BIP174/370/371 vectors.
- Fetch from GitHub at `cb9bc5f`, not from any scratch copy.
- **Cut imports.** Remove `LeanMiniscript.Bitcoin.ECDSA` and `LeanHash160`.
  - `validPublicKey` (`Psbt/Fields.lean:206-207`, which called `ECDSA.parsePublicKey`) takes the pubkey check from a capability structure defined in `bitcoin`. The app fills it from `secp256k1` (Phase 7a); tests fill it with a test implementation.
  - **Two checks** (owner decision 2026-10-21, `lck-decide-hybrid-pubkey-xgr`). The capability carries:
    - `isValidPubkey : ByteArray → Bool`, the strict rule (33-byte 02/03 or 65-byte 04), filled from `Secp256k1.isValidPubkey`. It checks `PSBT_IN_PARTIAL_SIG` keys (`Fields.lean:379`), as cyberkrill's rust-bitcoin 0.32.8 does (`bitcoin::PublicKey`, `psbt/map/input.rs:82`): a hybrid (06/07) key there is rejected, whatever its parity.
    - `compressPubkey : ByteArray → Option ByteArray`, libsecp256k1's own `ec_pubkey_parse` rule (33-byte 02/03, 65-byte 04, or a 65-byte 06/07 whose tag matches y's parity), returning the 33-byte compressed key. It checks `PSBT_IN_BIP32_DERIVATION` and `PSBT_OUT_BIP32_DERIVATION` keys (`Fields.lean:391`, `:487`): a matching-parity hybrid key is accepted and a mismatched one rejected, as rust-bitcoin does there (`secp256k1::PublicKey`, `psbt/map/input.rs:93`, `psbt/map/output.rs:40`). Upstream's `ECDSA.parsePublicKey` (`Bitcoin/ECDSA.lean:54`) accepted matching hybrids on all three key types.
    - The codec keeps every key as the raw bytes it read (`Fields.lean:380`, `:393`, `:489`) and detects duplicates on raw record keys (`Codec.lean:104-105`), as Bitcoin Core and btcd do. It does not rewrite a 04 or hybrid bip32 key to 33 bytes as rust-bitcoin does: no v1 command prints bip32 keys, and README says the library keeps the raw bytes. `parse cap hashes (serialize p) = .ok p` (Phase 4a, 3 of 3) is unchanged.
  - **Same-point check.** Add `Psbt.checkBip32SamePoint` (takes the capability, returns `Except PsbtError Unit`). Within one input's or one output's bip32 map, two keys with equal `compressPubkey` results (02-G with 04-G, or 04-G with 06-G) give a new structured error, `duplicateBip32Point`, carrying the map's scope and both raw keys. rust-bitcoin rejects such a map with `DuplicateKey`, because it keys the map by the parsed point (`psbt/macros.rs:100-106`). `parse` does not call it, so the library keeps Core's and btcd's raw-key behaviour and the Phase 4a (3 of 3) theorems are unchanged; the app calls it on every PSBT it parses where cyberkrill does (Phase 7c). `partial_sigs` get no such check: rust-bitcoin keys them by `bitcoin::PublicKey`, whose equality includes the compressed flag, so 02-G and 04-G there are distinct in both.
  - **New `secp256k1` function.** Phase 1a is closed, so this bead adds `Secp256k1.compressPubkey : ByteArray → Option ByteArray` to `packages/secp256k1`: a C function in `link_shim.c` that returns none unless the length is 33 or 65, then calls `secp256k1_ec_pubkey_parse` with no prefix check, then `secp256k1_ec_pubkey_serialize` with `SECP256K1_EC_COMPRESSED` (the serialize path `lck_secp_recover` already uses). `isValidPubkey` and `verify` stay strict. README's curve-interface table gains its row, and README's hybrid paragraph records the decision.
  - `bitcoin` must not import `secp256k1` (plan §2: pure packages never import an FFI package).
- **Hashing.** SHA-256 and SHA-256d go through `packages/sha256`.
  - `Bitcoin/Deserialization.lean` imports `doubleSHA256` from `LegacySighash.lean`. Re-home it onto `sha256d`, and copy no sighash code.
  - The RIPEMD160 and HASH160 preimage checks (`preimageHash`, `Fields.lean:272-276`) take their two hash functions as a **parameter**. Phase 4a (2 of 3) supplies our own RIPEMD-160 and HASH160 for it (owner decision, 2026-10-19). Tests in this bead pass a stand-in.
- **Reconcile CompactSize** with Phase 3a (1 of 4). This bead owns the final reconcile: `bitcoin` ends with one CompactSize codec, and README says which.
- **Tests.** Upstream's `Psbt/CodecExamples.lean` (22 `native_decide` uses) and `Psbt/FieldsExamples.lean` (3) become `lake test` checks. `native_decide` stays allowed only in test files (plan §6 default #3).
- **Attribution.** Upstream files carry no per-file header (`Psbt/Codec.lean:1` is an `import`). Give each copied file a first-line provenance comment (`Copied from febyeji/lean-miniscript @ cb9bc5f, <path>; MIT, see <notice file>`), never the dual-licence header. lean-miniscript's MIT notice (its `LICENSE`, "Copyright (c) 2026 Yeji Han") sits beside them.
  - The vector lists are BIP174/370/371 data (extracted by lean-miniscript's `scripts/generate_psbt_fixtures.py` from bitcoin/bips @ `927b6de9915c9262615a6399de51b200f81e5aa4`, `Psbt/Fixtures.lean:1-3`; BSD-2-Clause per the BIP headers there and at `130b8e0`), not lean-miniscript's own: their provenance line names lean-miniscript @ `cb9bc5f` as the route, bips @ `927b6de` as the source and BSD-2-Clause as the licence.

## Non-goals
- RIPEMD-160 and HASH160 (Phase 4a, 2 of 3). The new PSBT and transaction theorems (Phase 4a, 3 of 3).
- PSBT role modules (Creator, Updater, Signer, Combiner, Finalizer; 45 theorems upstream). v1 only parses PSBTs, and Core builds them (plan §1).
- Miniscript and descriptors. Signing and sighash code.

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- The parser returns structured errors for:
  - bad magic;
  - truncated input;
  - duplicate keys;
  - trailing data;
  - an invalid pubkey, through the capability (`isValidPubkey` for `partial_sigs` keys, `compressPubkey` for bip32 keys);
  - a preimage mismatch.
- `Psbt.checkBip32SamePoint` returns its own error, `duplicateBip32Point`, distinct from the raw `duplicateKey`.
- Upstream's `DeserializationProofs.lean` stays proven after the port. **Never weaken a stated obligation.** If one is out of reach, follow the common stop mechanics.
- **The fixtures file holds a tprv.** `Psbt/CodecExamples.lean:2` imports `LeanMiniscript.Psbt.Fixtures`, and `Psbt/Fixtures.lean:73` is `bip174MasterKey`, a tprv. Copy from `Psbt/Fixtures.lean` only the vector lists `bip174Invalid`, `bip174Valid`, `bip174SignerFailures`, `bip174Roles` (PSBT strings only; `CodecExamples.lean:45-46` parse them), the `bip370*`/`bip371*` lists and `bip370Locktimes`.
  - Do **not** copy `bip174MasterKey` (L73) or the Creator/Updater fixtures (L75-94). Role tests (`RoleExamples.lean`) are not ported.
  - Add to `ci.yml` and to `bitcoin`'s `lake test` a key-shaped grep: `grep -rEn --exclude-dir=.lake '[tx]prv[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{100,}'` over `packages` (from the repo root) or `..` (from `packages/bitcoin`, the test's working directory). The pattern matches key-shaped strings only, not the word "xprv" in prose.
  - Do not write it as `! grep …`: grep exits 2 on a missing path and `!` turns that into a pass. grep exit 1 is a pass; 0 or 2 fails the check. GitHub's bash runs with `-e`, so in `ci.yml` write it as `rc=0; grep -rEn --exclude-dir=.lake '[tx]prv[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{100,}' packages || rc=$?; test "$rc" -eq 1`. Watch the gate go red once on a planted key-shaped string in a temp copy.

## Dependencies / ordering
- Plan §4: Phase 4 depends on Phase 3a, so this bead waits for all four Phase 3a beads.
- Phase 4a (2 of 3) and Phase 4a (3 of 3) wait for this bead.

title: Phase 4c: SLIP-132 version-byte table and extended-key conversion (library only)
description:
## Outcome
`packages/bitcoin` has cyberkrill's SLIP-132 version-byte table and converts an extended public key string between its SLIP-132 prefixes. There are no multisig or private forms. The conversion round-trip is proven.

## Why this exists
The v1 scope lists SLIP-132. Its only cyberkrill caller is the Trezor code (`trezor.rs:12,196`), which is out of v1. Plan §6 default #1, approved: it ships as a library function with vectors but **no CLI command**.

## Scope
- The version table, mirroring `slip132.rs:9-20`.
- Conversion over Base58Check, Phase 3a (2 of 4): decode, check the version bytes are known, swap them, re-encode.

- A CLI command.
- BIP32 derivation.
- Multisig and private-key prefixes. `slip132.rs` has none.

  - **cyberkrill goldens for the converted forms** (AGENTS.md "Reference only"). cyberkrill has no SLIP-132 command, and `slip132` compiles only with feature `trezor` (`cyberkrill-core/src/lib.rs:10-11`; a default feature, `Cargo.toml:12`). A committed script clones `27cad1f` into a temp dir and appends a temporary `#[test]` to `slip132.rs`'s `mod tests` that prints `parse_slip132_xpub(s)?.to_string()` (`slip132.rs:54-62`, which calls `from_slip132_str`, `:31-50`; both pure) for each converted string.   - **Fallback, not a stop.** If the clone does not build within 30 minutes, the expectation is the `python3Packages.base58` cross-check below plus the version-swap rule read from `slip132.rs:31-50`. README marks it hand-derived and says why no cyberkrill golden was produced.

title: Phase 4d: P2WPKH weight and fee estimation ported exactly from cyberkrill
description:
## Outcome
`packages/bitcoin` estimates transaction weight and fee exactly as cyberkrill does. Weight and vbytes are exact integers. The fee reproduces cyberkrill's one floating-point product bit for bit and is returned as a whole-sat `Amount` (Phase 3a, 1 of 4).

## Why this exists
`onchain-create-psbt` and `onchain-move-utxos` compute fees locally (plan §3, "Local weight and fee estimation"). The port must produce the same fee as cyberkrill on the same inputs. Phase 8c uses this estimator, in both of its beads.

## Scope
Port `cyberkrill-core/src/bitcoin_rpc.rs:982-997` @ `27cad1f` exactly:
- `estimate_transaction_weight` (`:984-993`) assumes every input is rust-bitcoin's `InputWeightPrediction::P2WPKH_MAX` (`:986`) and every output script is 22 bytes (`:990`).
  - `P2WPKH_MAX` and the weight-prediction formula come from the rust-bitcoin crate version that cyberkrill's `Cargo.lock` pins (0.32.8 at the time of transfer), not from cyberkrill's own source. Read that crate's source, at that exact version, for the constant and the formula.
  - The comment at `:988` says "= 21 bytes"; the code's 22 is right, since it includes the push byte.
- `calculate_fee_with_feerate` (`:997-1006`): `vbytes = weight.div_ceil(4)`, and fee = `(vbytes as f64 * sat_per_vb).round() as u64` (`:1002`), with `sat_per_vb = rate.as_fractional_sats()` = msats as f64 / 1000.0 (`:192-194`; called at `:969` and `:1370-1371`).
  - Reproduce that arithmetic bit for bit with Lean `Float` (IEEE binary64, the same operations in the same order): `(vbytes.toFloat * (rateMsat.toFloat / 1000.0)).round`, then `Float.toUInt64`, which saturates like Rust's `as u64` (`lean_float_to_uint64` in `include/lean/lean.h`). `Float.round` is `@[extern "round"]` (`Init/Data/Float/Float.lean:525`), C `round`, which rounds half away from zero like Rust's `f64::round`.
  - Exact arithmetic would differ: 110 vB at `1.15sats` is `126.49999999999999` in binary64, so cyberkrill charges 126 sats where the exact 126.5 rounds to 127. A fee rate is not an amount, so plan §3 "port it exactly" wins here. README says that the fee path uses binary64 on purpose.
- **The rate's units.** `--fee-rate` and `--fee` parse as cyberkrill's `AmountInput` (`bitcoin_rpc.rs:219-283`), so a bare number is **BTC**: `--fee-rate 15` means 1.5e9 sat/vB, despite the help text's "'15'" (`main.rs:920`, `:992`, `:1046`), and a sats rate is rounded to msat through `f64` (`:122`). This estimator takes the rate in msat per vB; the commands (Phase 8c) parse it with Phase 3a (1 of 4)'s CLI grammar.

## Non-goals
- Input selection. `move_utxos`'s largest-first selection belongs to Phase 8c (2 of 2).
- Fee-rate fetching. Any "improvement" to the estimate: exactness to cyberkrill is the requirement.

## Dependencies / ordering
- Plan §4: Phase 4 depends on Phase 3a, so this bead waits for all four Phase 3a beads.
- Unblocks Phase 8. `onchain-create-psbt` (Phase 8c, 1 of 2) and `onchain-move-utxos` (Phase 8c, 2 of 2) use it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Weight matches cyberkrill's test values. `test_transaction_weight_estimation` (`bitcoin_rpc.rs:1927`, body from `:1928`) asserts vbyte **ranges**, not exact values: (1 in, 1 out) 109..=112; (2, 2) 206..=212; (5, 1) 378..=385.
  - The port's exact results must fall inside them.
  - Pin the exact vbytes the rust-bitcoin formula gives for those cases, as computed by cyberkrill @ `27cad1f`. Get them through a temporary test in a throwaway clone (AGENTS.md "Reference only"): `estimate_transaction_weight` is private and pure, so the test goes in `bitcoin_rpc.rs`'s own `mod tests`, built inside that commit's own `nix develop` with dependencies fetched first, and run offline inside `unshare -rn sh -c 'ip link set lo up && …'` with `HOME` set to a temp dir. If the clone does not build, derive them by hand from rust-bitcoin 0.32.8's `P2WPKH_MAX` (`src/blockdata/transaction.rs:1521`) and `predict_weight_internal` (`:1428`), write the arithmetic in README, and mark them hand-derived (an off-line check gave 438 WU / 110 vB, 834 / 209 and 1526 / 382).
- The fee matches cyberkrill on a few fee rates, including fractional ones given as cyberkrill takes them (for example `2.5sats`).
- A pinned test: 110 vB at `1.15sats` gives 126 sats, as in cyberkrill.
### Common definition of done (plan §4, every work session)
- `nix build` and `nix flake check` exit 0. The flake check runs `lake build && lake test` for every package listed in `lakePackages` in `flake.nix`, inside the nix sandbox, then runs the app. Stage new files (`git add`) before running `nix flake check`: a flake sees only tracked files.
- In each touched package, `nix develop -c lake build` and `nix develop -c lake test` exit 0.
- No `sorry`: `grep -rnw sorry --include='*.lean' --exclude-dir=.lake packages` prints nothing (CI runs the same check from Phase 2 on).
- `#print axioms` on every theorem this bead lists shows only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. Each listed theorem is added to the package's committed axiom-gate test (Phase 2's pattern); `lake test` fails on any axiom outside the three. The gate is an allowlist of those three and contains no "sorry" substring. No `native_decide` in library or proof modules; test files may use it.
- The vector counts this bead states pass. Each test asserts that the number of vectors it loaded equals a pinned constant, so a dropped vector fails, and the test output prints each count (for example `<set> valid: N/N`).
- `README.md` is updated: what the package now provides, vector sources and counts, and anything this bead says to document.
- `AGENTS.md` rules hold, including "Reference only" for any value taken from cyberkrill. New Lean, C and script files we write carry the dual-licence header; third-party and copied files follow the rule below, and JSON and other formats without comments need none.
- **Safety.** Tests use only published vectors, published test mnemonics, the BOLT #11 specification's published example private key (tests only), recordings from a throwaway regtest node, and synthetic or script-generated fixtures under the third-party rule (for example cyberkrill's captured outputs on those inputs, synthetic provider responses, our own LNURL and LUD JSON, values a committed script derives from published inputs). Never anything from the owner's node, wallets or devices. Tests never reach the internet, port 8332 or `~/.bitcoin`. Nothing committed contains private keys, seeds, xprvs, tprvs or WIF keys, or real addresses, xpubs or device dumps, apart from that BOLT #11 example key. No hardware wallets, no signing outside test vectors, no broadcast, no mainnet funds.
- **Third-party material** (`AGENTS.md` "Licence", plan §5):
  - Admitted in the tree, each with a provenance sidecar or header line (source URL, commit, path, licence), never the dual-licence header: MIT, BSD, ISC, CC0 or public domain, and CC-BY-4.0 (attribution and a note of any changes, for example "extracted and reformatted", kept in the sidecar). Material offered under a choice that includes MIT (such as fedimint-lite's `MIT OR Apache-2.0`) is taken under MIT.
  - Kept out of the tree: Apache-2.0-only, share-alike (CC-BY-SA) and unlicensed material. Use a pinned non-flake input read at test time, or replace it with vectors we generate ourselves.
  - Copied code whose upstream file has no header gets a provenance comment (upstream repo, commit, path, "MIT") with the upstream MIT notice in a file beside it, never the dual-licence header.
  - In a Lean file the provenance line is the first line and a `--` line comment (or `/- … -/`), never a `/-! … -/` doc comment, for example `-- Copied from <repo> @ <commit>, <path>; MIT, see <notice file>`. JSON and other formats without comments get the sidecar.
- **Stop mechanics.** If this bead says stop and report: commit no weakened statement, `br defer` the bead, add label `owner-decision`, comment what was tried (`br comments add`), and end the work session blocked.
- **Follow-ups.** A delta or stricter check you think v1 needs goes in a new bead created deferred with label `owner-decision`, and in README "Deltas not taken". Never implement it unranked.
- **Upstream fixes.** A fix that would also help upstream (lean4-hash, lean-miniscript) goes in the committed `docs/upstream-fixes.md` (file, problem, fix), not in a br comment. Phase 10a (3 of 3) turns that file into patches.

## Spec refs
