title: Phase 8a (2 of 2): Bitcoin Core JSON-RPC client, auth and the shared RPC flags, with replay tests
description:
## Outcome
The app has a Bitcoin Core JSON-RPC client over `http-curl`, with cookie and user/password auth matching cyberkrill, and the shared RPC flag group. Every RPC call v1 makes is exercised against Phase 8a (1 of 2)'s recordings on Phase 1b (2 of 2)'s localhost stub.

## Why this exists
Phases 8b, 8c and 9d build on this client. Phase 8a is split in two to keep each work session small: the recording generator and recordings (1 of 2), then this client.

## Scope
- **Client** (cyberkrill `cyberkrill-core/src/bitcoin_rpc.rs` @ `27cad1f`):
  - JSON-RPC POST with basic auth (`rpc_call` `:429-466`); a non-2xx reply is an HTTP error (`:449-453`), and a non-null `error` field is an RPC error (`:456-460`). Core 28 and later return RPC errors with HTTP 200 (Phase 8a, 1 of 2).
  - **Auth, matching cyberkrill:**
    - user and password are used only when both are set (`:366-377`);
    - the cookie is read from `<bitcoin-dir>/.cookie` and split on the first `:` (`:379-388`, `:407-427`);
    - `new_auto` tries the cookie only when `--bitcoin-dir` is given, and otherwise falls back to user/password or no auth (`:390-405`);
    - it also falls back silently when the cookie is unreadable (`:397-398`), which means no auth when no user/password is set;
    - `--rpc-user`/`--rpc-password` conflict with `--bitcoin-dir` (`main.rs:850-854` and siblings);
    - despite the help text's "default: ~/.bitcoin", there is no default dir on the RPC path: `main.rs:1553`, `1680`, `1800` and `1939` pass `args.bitcoin_dir.as_ref().map(Path::new)`, which is `None` when the flag is absent. Match the code, and note the help-text discrepancy in README.
  - Parse Core's JSON amounts exactly into `Amount`, through `Lean.JsonNumber` (mantissa, exponent), never `Float`.
- **Shared RPC flags.** Add the RPC-connection flag group (`--rpc-url`, `--bitcoin-dir`, `--rpc-user`, `--rpc-password`) to Phase 7a's parser once, for the Phase 8 commands to share, and test the `--bitcoin-dir` conflict there.
- **Missing recordings.** If a test needs a request no recording holds, add a case to Phase 8a (1 of 2)'s case file and re-run the generator for the new case only (`--cases <new>`; regtest only, same safety rules), committing its new recording file. Never hand-write one.
- **The full RPC list** (plan §3), one wrapper per call Phase 8a (1 of 2) recorded: `listunspent`, `scantxoutset`, `getdescriptorinfo`, `deriveaddresses`, `createpsbt`, `walletcreatefundedpsbt`, `importdescriptors` (`:764`), `getblockchaininfo` (`:725`), `getreceivedbyaddress` (`:1172`), `getrawtransaction` (`:1310`), plus `getblock`, which only `onchain-dca-report` needs (Phase 9d; `dca_report.rs:204`).
  - `list_unspent_for_descriptor` imports the descriptor into the node's wallet: timestamp `now`, no rescan (`:753`), errors ignored (`:774`). Keep that behaviour and document it in README, including that funds older than the import may be missed.
- Replay tests for every call, through the client, against the stub.

## Non-goals
- The recording generator and the recordings (Phase 8a, 1 of 2).
- The command handlers themselves (Phases 8b and 8c).
- BDK backends, `--electrum` and `--esplora` (out of v1).

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- Tests replay recordings only. Nothing here runs `bitcoind` or reaches port 8332 or `~/.bitcoin`.
- **Connection rule** (Phases 8b, 8c, 9a, 9b, 9c and 9d follow it). The host-side `nix develop -c lake test` has no network namespace, and the default RPC URL is `http://127.0.0.1:8332` (`main.rs:11`; DCA hardcodes it, `dca_report.rs:170`). So:
  - every app test that opens a connection passes the stub's URL explicitly: in process as the client's URL argument (Phase 9d through Phase 9a (1 of 2)'s override parameter), or as `--rpc-url` to a spawned binary;
  - the test helper that spawns the binary refuses to start it: (i) for `onchain-list-utxos`, `onchain-create-psbt`, `onchain-create-funded-psbt` or `onchain-move-utxos` unless `--rpc-url` is given and names the stub's port, since the default is `http://127.0.0.1:8332` (`main.rs:11`); (ii) for `onchain-dca-report`, whose RPC URL is hardcoded (`dca_report.rs:170`); (iii) for any amount-taking argument (an `--outputs` entry's amount, `--max-amount`, the amount of `convert-amount` or `ln-generate-invoice`) that cyberkrill would read as fiat: the text after its last digit, `.` or `,`, trimmed, is exactly three ASCII letters other than `btc` or `sat`, in any case (`parse_fiat_amount`, `main.rs:193-206`; `sats`, `msat` and `msats` are bitcoin units, `is_bitcoin_amount_unit`), since fiat feed URLs are hardcoded (`price_feed.rs:268-459`); (iv) when any URL argument of the spawned command (`--rpc-url`, or a URL inside another argument such as an invite or a Lightning address) names port 8332. Each refusal is tested. Paths (ii) and (iii) are tested in process instead (Phases 9a, 9b and 9d), through Phase 9a (1 of 2)'s app entry point, which takes the test URL override and returns the exit code and the stderr text; that entry point's own refusal (every override URL must name `127.0.0.1` and a port other than 8332) is built and tested in Phase 9a (1 of 2), not here; this bead does not depend on it;
  - the default URL is tested only as a parsed value, never by connecting;
  - in the dev shell, every spawned test that opens a connection runs inside `unshare -rn sh -c 'ip link set lo up && …'`: the test driver re-execs itself once through `unshare -rn sh -c 'ip link set lo up && exec "$0" "$@"'`, with a marker variable that stops a second re-exec. Where `unshare -rn` is unavailable, those tests print `SKIP (no unshare)` and do not run. Only inside the check derivation, whose sandbox has no network, do they run without `unshare`: this bead sets a marker variable for that in the check derivation (`flake.nix`). They never run unguarded. Add `pkgs.util-linux` (for `unshare`) and `pkgs.iproute2` (for `ip`) to `devShells.default` if absent. A guard that cannot bring `lo` up fails the test; only a missing or refused `unshare -rn` gives `SKIP (no unshare)`.
- Never log or echo the cookie or the RPC password in errors.

## Dependencies / ordering
- Depends on Phase 8a (1 of 2), which carries Phase 8's upstream dependencies (both Phase 1b beads, every Phase 4 bead, Phases 7a-7c).
- Phase 8b, both Phase 8c beads and Phase 9d wait for both Phase 8a beads. Phases 9b and 9c wait for this bead, for the connection rule.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every RPC call in the list above, `getblock` included, is exercised against its recorded response on the localhost stub.
- Cookie auth and user/password auth are both tested against Phase 8a (1 of 2)'s fixed throwaway credentials, including the both-must-be-set rule, the unreadable-cookie fallback and the conflict with `--bitcoin-dir`.
- An auth failure (401 from the stub) is reported clearly, and so is an RPC `error` object in an HTTP 200 reply. The 401 tests use a wrong password and a cookie file holding a wrong one.
- Each of the spawn helper's four refusals is tested, and so is the dev-shell guard: with `unshare` unavailable and no check-derivation marker, a spawned network test prints `SKIP (no unshare)` and does not run. The `nix flake check` log shows those tests ran there, with no `SKIP (no unshare)` line.
- If this bead added recording cases, `git diff --stat` against the branch base over `packages/cyberkrill/test/recordings` lists only the new case files.
### Common definition of done (plan §4, every work session)

title: Phase 8c (2 of 2): onchain-move-utxos over Core RPC, with local selection and fee; the output is the selected total minus the fee
description:
## Outcome
`onchain-move-utxos` (`main.rs:1834`; `bitcoin_rpc.rs:1286`; JSON `PsbtResponse`) works over Core RPC on the recorded regtest fixtures. It keeps cyberkrill's local largest-first selection and fee, and its output is the **full selected total minus the fee**, so the excess over `--max-amount` is never silently given to the miner. The `--descriptor` + `--bitcoin-dir` BDK combination and `--wallet-file` are rejected.

## Why this exists
This is a v1 Core RPC command (plan §4, Phase 8). Owner decision (2026-10-19), which closed the `--max-amount` question bead:
- cyberkrill's Core path clamps the total to the cap (`selected_value.min(max_btc)`, `bitcoin_rpc.rs:1354`) and outputs total minus fee (`:1390`, `:1401`), with no change output. Any selected amount above `--max-amount` therefore becomes miner fee.
- The port keeps the selection, but outputs the selected total minus the fee, with no clamp to the cap. That matches cyberkrill's BDK path (`bdk_wallet.rs:854-900`), which spends the whole selection.
- It is a documented, tested difference from cyberkrill's Core path, one of the three exceptions to the golden rule (Phase 7a), and is reported upstream as douglaz/cyberkrill#152.

Phase 8c is split in two to keep each work session small; this part does not depend on the other.

## Scope
- **Flags:** `--inputs` (required), `--destination` (required), exactly one of `--fee-rate` or `--fee` (`main.rs:1841`), `--max-amount` (floored to the sat, `main.rs:1887`; a non-zero `--max-amount` below 1 sat exits non-zero, `:373-380`; Phase 7a defines that FloorSat helper; reuse it), `--network` (validated; a bad value exits non-zero, `main.rs:1848-1856`), `-o`, `--psbt-output`.
- **Fee units.** `--fee-rate` and `--fee` parse with Phase 3a (1 of 4)'s CLI amount grammar, as cyberkrill's `AmountInput`: a bare number is BTC, so `--fee-rate 15` means 1.5e9 sat/vB despite the help text's "'15'" (`main.rs:1046`). Match the code, and note the help-text discrepancy in README.
- **Calls.** It first expands descriptor-style inputs through `parse_and_expand_inputs` (`bitcoin_rpc.rs:1295`, `:854-899`), which calls `list_unspent_for_descriptor` (`:771`): `getdescriptorinfo` and `importdescriptors` (`:741`, `:764`; errors ignored, `:774`), then `getdescriptorinfo`, `deriveaddresses` (100 addresses) and `listunspent` (`:819`, `:835`, `:496`). Then it calls `getrawtransaction` verbose for each input (`:1310`; this needs txindex or a wallet transaction), then `createpsbt` (`:1415`) with locktime 0 and replaceable false (`:1409`, `:1412`).
- **Selection** when `--max-amount` is set (`:1329-1345`): sort by value, largest first, and add inputs until the selected total reaches or exceeds the cap (the cap is tested before each input is added, `:1340`, so a cap of 0 selects nothing and the command exits non-zero as at `:1347-1352`). The sort is stable (`sort_by`, `:1333`): ties keep input order. Use exact `Amount`, not `f64` (plan §3). With no `--max-amount`, every input is spent.
- **Output:** the selected total minus the fee, with no clamp to `--max-amount`. A non-positive result is an error, as at `:1391`.
- **Fee:** `--fee-rate` through Phase 4d's estimator (the input count, one output); `--fee` as an absolute amount.
- `--psbt-output` writes the PSBT file as cyberkrill does. Validate the PSBT (`:1423`) with the app's PSBT parse (Phase 7c: Phase 4a's parser, then `Psbt.checkBip32SamePoint`).
- **Rejections** (plan §3, §6 default #5): `--descriptor` + `--bitcoin-dir` (`main.rs:1871-1873`) and `--wallet-file` get a clear message. Handle `--electrum` and `--esplora` as Phase 7a settled.
  - cyberkrill sends `--wallet-file` + `--bitcoin-dir` to BDK too, and with no `--bitcoin-dir` it reads the wallet file and then ignores it, running Core with no descriptor (`main.rs:1859-1881`). The port rejects both; list them under README "Deltas taken" with that code path.
  - `--descriptor` without `--bitcoin-dir` is likewise accepted and then ignored (same lines). Accept and ignore it as cyberkrill does, or reject it and list it under "Deltas taken".
- **Fiat `--max-amount`** arrives in Phase 9a (2 of 2). Until then, fiat input gives a clear "not yet supported" error.
- README lists the output rule under "Deltas taken", with the issue link.

## Non-goals
- `onchain-create-psbt` and `onchain-create-funded-psbt` (Phase 8c, 1 of 2).
- A change output. Signing, finalizing or broadcasting, ever. BDK.

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- Exact `Amount` everywhere. Any other result that differs from cyberkrill's `f64` arithmetic is listed in README's exact-amounts section and the golden allowlist.
- PSBTs in tests come only from the regtest recordings.
- **Never run cyberkrill on a BDK-route combination:** `--descriptor` or `--wallet-file` with `--bitcoin-dir` (`main.rs:1859-1873`), `--electrum` or `--esplora`. Its BDK bitcoind route hardcodes `http://127.0.0.1:8332` and ignores `--rpc-url` (`cyberkrill-core/src/bdk_wallet.rs:254-259`). Rejection tests are port-only, and README cites the code path.
- **Capture safety**, as in Phase 8b: every capture runs inside `unshare -rn sh -c 'ip link set lo up && …'` with the stub started in the same namespace, passes an explicit stub `--rpc-url`, runs with `HOME` set to a temp dir, and aborts if anything other than the stub listens on the port.
- **Port tests** follow Phase 8a (2 of 2)'s connection rule: an explicit stub URL on every test that connects, and a spawn helper that refuses unguarded endpoints.
- **Missing recordings.** If a test needs a request no recording holds (each fee case changes `createpsbt`'s output amount, `bitcoin_rpc.rs:1388-1401`), including the no-clamp delta case, add a case to Phase 8a (1 of 2)'s case file and re-run the generator for the new case only (`--cases <new>`; regtest only, same safety rules), committing its new recording file. Never hand-write one.

## Dependencies / ordering
- Depends on both Phase 8a beads, which carry Phase 8's upstream dependencies, including Phase 4d's estimator, and on the `--max-amount` decision bead (closed).
- Phase 9a (2 of 2), Phase 10a (1 of 3) and Phase 10a (3 of 3) wait for both Phase 8c beads.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Replay tests on the stub, with JSON values compared against cyberkrill @ `27cad1f` on the same recordings, wherever cyberkrill's clamp does not apply: no `--max-amount`, and a cap at or above the selected total. Where cyberkrill's `f64` params and the port's exact params differ, the test also asserts the port's exact params.

- Descriptor-style inputs expand through the recorded calls, and equal-value inputs keep their input order.

## Scope
- **`onchain-create-psbt`.**
  - `--inputs` (required, repeatable; descriptor-style inputs expand through `list_unspent_for_descriptor`, `:771`), `--outputs` (required), `--fee-rate`, `--network` (validated; a bad value exits non-zero, `main.rs:1605`), `-o`, `--psbt-output`.
  - It calls `createpsbt` (`:955`).
  - The fee is a local estimate from Phase 4d (`:984`) and is never deducted (`:967-979`); keep that.
  - It validates the PSBT (`:1010`) with the app's PSBT parse (Phase 7c: Phase 4a's parser, then `Psbt.checkBip32SamePoint`).
- **`onchain-create-funded-psbt`.**
  - `--inputs` (required on the RPC route, `main.rs:1749`), `--outputs`, `--conf-target`, `--estimate-mode`, `--fee-rate`, `--network` (validated as above, `main.rs:1715`), `-o`, `--psbt-output`.
  - A change probe runs only for `<0;1>` inputs: `getdescriptorinfo` (`:1109`), `deriveaddresses` (`:1120`), `getreceivedbyaddress` (`:1172`), with a fallback to `listunspent` (`:1142`). Then it calls `walletcreatefundedpsbt` (`:1260`) and validates the returned PSBT (`:1269`) with the app's PSBT parse (Phase 7c).
  - Core does coin selection here; this is the only command that leaves selection to Core (plan §3).
- `--psbt-output` writes the PSBT file as cyberkrill does.
- **`--outputs`** parses as `parse_outputs` and `parse_output_list` (`main.rs:2013-2067`, `split_output_parts` `:2192`) on both commands. A BTC entry that is not a whole number of sats exits non-zero before any price lookup (`:2033-2036`, `ensure_whole_sat_output_amount` `:2207-2219`). Phase 7a defines that whole-sat check; reuse it.
- **Fee-rate units.** `--fee-rate` parses with Phase 3a (1 of 4)'s CLI amount grammar, as cyberkrill's `AmountInput`: a bare number is BTC, so `--fee-rate 15` means 1.5e9 sat/vB despite the help text's "'15'" (`main.rs:920`, `:992`). Match the code, and note the help-text discrepancy in README.
- **Rejections** (plan §3, §6 default #5): `--descriptor` + `--bitcoin-dir` (`main.rs:1628-1630`, `:1738-1740`) and `--wallet-file` on both commands get a clear message.
  - cyberkrill sends `--wallet-file` + `--bitcoin-dir` to BDK too, and with no `--bitcoin-dir` it reads the wallet file and then ignores it, running Core with no descriptor (`main.rs:1617-1638`, `:1726-1748`). The port rejects both; list them under README "Deltas taken" with those code paths.
  - `--descriptor` without `--bitcoin-dir` is likewise accepted and then ignored on both commands (same lines). Accept and ignore it as cyberkrill does, or reject it and list it under "Deltas taken".
  - `--electrum` and `--esplora` are not ported. Handle them as Phase 7a settled.
- **Fiat output amounts.** `--outputs` accepts fiat in cyberkrill, but that arrives in Phase 9a (2 of 2). Until then, fiat input gives a clear "not yet supported" error.

## Non-goals
- `onchain-move-utxos` (Phase 8c, 2 of 2).
- Signing, finalizing or broadcasting. Never.
- BDK.

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- Exact `Amount` everywhere. Any result that differs from cyberkrill's `f64` arithmetic is listed in README's exact-amounts section and the golden allowlist.
- PSBTs in tests come only from the regtest recordings.
- **Never run cyberkrill on a BDK-route combination:** `--descriptor` or `--wallet-file` with `--bitcoin-dir` (`main.rs:1617-1630`, `:1726-1740`), `--electrum` or `--esplora`. Its BDK bitcoind route hardcodes `http://127.0.0.1:8332` and ignores `--rpc-url` (`cyberkrill-core/src/bdk_wallet.rs:254-259`). Rejection tests are port-only, and README cites the code path.
- **Capture safety**, as in Phase 8b: every capture runs inside `unshare -rn sh -c 'ip link set lo up && …'` with the stub started in the same namespace, passes an explicit stub `--rpc-url`, runs with `HOME` set to a temp dir, and aborts if anything other than the stub listens on the port. It passes `--bitcoin-dir` at a temp copy of Phase 8a (1 of 2)'s committed cookie fixture where the flags allow it, and `--rpc-user lck --rpc-password lck-throwaway` otherwise.
- **Port tests** follow Phase 8a (2 of 2)'s connection rule: an explicit stub URL on every test that connects, and a spawn helper that refuses unguarded endpoints.
- **Missing recordings.** If a test needs a request no recording holds (an `--outputs` set, a fee case), add a case to Phase 8a (1 of 2)'s case file and re-run the generator for the new case only (`--cases <new>`; regtest only, same safety rules), committing its new recording file. Never hand-write one.

## Dependencies / ordering
- Depends on both Phase 8a beads, which carry Phase 8's upstream dependencies, including Phase 4d's estimator.
- Phase 9a (2 of 2), Phase 10a (1 of 3) and Phase 10a (3 of 3) wait for both Phase 8c beads.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Replay tests on the stub for each command, with JSON values compared against cyberkrill @ `27cad1f` on the same recordings. Where cyberkrill's `f64` params and the port's exact params differ, the test also asserts the port's exact params.
- `onchain-create-psbt`'s local fee matches cyberkrill on the fixtures, with fee rates given as cyberkrill takes them (for example `2.5sats`).
- A bad `--network` value exits non-zero on both commands.
- The `<0;1>` change probe and its `listunspent` fallback are both exercised.
- Every BDK-combination and `--wallet-file` rejection is tested.
- The `--outputs` grammar and the whole-sat rule are tested: a BTC entry that is not a whole number of sats exits non-zero.
- If this bead added recording cases, `git diff --stat` against the branch base over `packages/cyberkrill/test/recordings` lists only the new case files.
### Common definition of done (plan §4, every work session)
- `nix build` and `nix flake check` exit 0. The flake check runs `lake build && lake test` for every package listed in `lakePackages` in `flake.nix`, inside the nix sandbox, then runs the app. Stage new files (`git add`) before running `nix flake check`: a flake sees only tracked files.
- In each touched package, `nix develop -c lake build` and `nix develop -c lake test` exit 0.
- No `sorry`: `grep -rnw sorry --include='*.lean' --exclude-dir=.lake packages` prints nothing (CI runs the same check from Phase 2 on).
- `#print axioms` on every theorem this bead lists shows only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. Each listed theorem is added to the package's committed axiom-gate test (Phase 2's pattern); `lake test` fails on any axiom outside the three. The gate is an allowlist of those three and contains no "sorry" substring. No `native_decide` in library or proof modules; test files may use it.
- The vector counts this bead states pass. Each test asserts that the number of vectors it loaded equals a pinned constant, so a dropped vector fails, and the test output prints each count (for example `<set> valid: N/N`).
- `README.md` is updated: what the package now provides, vector sources and counts, and anything this bead says to document.
- `AGENTS.md` rules hold, including "Reference only" for any value taken from cyberkrill. New Lean, C and script files we write carry the dual-licence header; third-party and copied files follow the rule below, and JSON and other formats without comments need none.
- **Safety.** Tests use only published vectors, published test mnemonics, the BOLT #11 specification's published example private key (tests only), recordings from a throwaway regtest node, and synthetic or script-generated fixtures under the third-party rule (for example cyberkrill's captured outputs on those inputs, synthetic provider responses, our own LNURL and LUD JSON, values a committed script derives from published inputs). Never anything from the owner's node, wallets or devices. Tests never reach the internet, port 8332 or `~/.bitcoin`. Nothing committed contains private keys, seeds, xprvs, tprvs or WIF keys, or real addresses, xpubs or device dumps, apart from that BOLT #11 example key. No hardware wallets, no signing outside test vectors, no broadcast, no mainnet funds.
- **Third-party material** (`AGENTS.md` "Licence", plan §5):
  - Admitted in the tree, each with a provenance sidecar or header line (source URL, commit, path, licence), never the dual-licence header: MIT, BSD, ISC, CC0 or public domain, and CC-BY-4.0 (attribution and a note of any changes, for example "extracted and reformatted", kept in the sidecar). Material offered under a choice that includes MIT (such as fedimint-lite's `MIT OR Apache-2.0`) is taken under MIT.
  - Kept out of the tree: Apache-2.0-only, share-alike (CC-BY-SA) and unlicensed material. Use a pinned non-flake input read at test time, or replace it with vectors we generate ourselves.
  - Copied code whose upstream file has no header gets a provenance comment (upstream repo, commit, path, "MIT") with the upstream MIT notice in a file beside it, never the dual-licence header.
  - In a Lean file the provenance line is the first line and a `--` line comment (or `/- … -/`), never a `/-! … -/` doc comment, for example `-- Copied from <repo> @ <commit>, <path>; MIT, see <notice file>`. JSON and other formats without comments get the sidecar.
- **Stop mechanics.** If this bead says stop and report: commit no weakened statement, `br defer` the bead, add label `owner-decision`, comment what was tried (`br comments add`), and end the work session blocked.
- **Follow-ups.** A delta or stricter check you think v1 needs goes in a new bead created deferred with label `owner-decision`, and in README "Deltas not taken". Never implement it unranked.
- **Upstream fixes.** A fix that would also help upstream (lean4-hash, lean-miniscript) goes in the committed `docs/upstream-fixes.md` (file, problem, fix), not in a br comment. Phase 10a (3 of 3) turns that file into patches.

title: Phase 9a (1 of 2): price feeds and median, the exact fiat type and precision modes, the test URL override, and convert-amount with fiat
description:
## Outcome
The app fetches BTC prices from cyberkrill's public price feeds over `http-curl` and aggregates them exactly as cyberkrill does. It has the exact fiat amount type and applies cyberkrill's three precision modes (WholeSat and FloorSat are Phase 7a's helpers), and it has the test-only URL override. `convert-amount` accepts fiat input.

`ln-generate-invoice` (Phase 9b) uses the same path. The fiat amounts on the three onchain commands are Phase 9a (2 of 2).

## Why this exists
This is a v1 network feature (plan §4, Phase 9). Plan §3 asked Phase 9 to settle the feed count against the code.

Phase 9a is split in two to keep each work session small, and so that Phase 9b does not wait for Phase 8c: this part needs no Core RPC command.

## Scope
- **Feeds** (`cyberkrill-core/src/price_feed.rs` @ `27cad1f`). Nine feeds, run in parallel (`:67-118`), each with an 8-second timeout (`:62`):
  - CoinGecko simple/price (`:268`), Coinbase exchange-rates (`:290`), blockchain.info ticker (`:313`);
  - Kraken Ticker (`:332`), Fedi `price-feed.dev.fedibtc.com/latest` (`:13`, used at `:354`), CEX.io (`:373`);
  - Bitstamp v2 (`:402`), Yadio (`:430`), Gemini v1 pubticker (`:459`).
  - A 404 from CEX.io, Bitstamp, Yadio or Gemini counts as "no quote", not an error.
- **Aggregation** (`aggregate_btc_price` `:140`):
  - fail if fewer than 3 feeds succeed (`:144-150`);
  - sort by price, then name (`:152`);
  - the median (`:251-263`) is the middle value for an odd count and the mean of the two middle values for an even count;
  - warn on stderr when the spread is over 2% (`:11`, `:182`), and report per-feed issues on stderr (`:132`).
- **Feed count, settled here as plan §3 asked.** The code uses 9 feeds with a quorum of 3. `convert-amount`'s long help (`main.rs:529-533`) says "median of 5", which is stale.
  - Match the code's behaviour. Correcting the help text is a delta: list it in README's "Deltas taken".
- **Exactness.** This bead owns the exact fiat amount type. Prices are parsed from JSON without `Float`.
  - cyberkrill converts in `f64` as `round(amount / price * 1e11)` msat, with a "less than 1 msat" error (`price_feed.rs:228-249`). The port computes the msat value exactly from the exact median and rounds half away from zero to the msat, then applies the flag's precision mode.
  - The three modes, as in cyberkrill's `FiatConversionPrecision` (`main.rs:50-54`, `:349-380`):
    - **Millisat** for `convert-amount` and `ln-generate-invoice` (`:73`, `:88`);
    - **WholeSat**, half-up, for fiat `--outputs` entries (`:2051`, `:360-371`), followed by whole-sat enforcement (`:2059-2061`, `:2207-2219`);
    - **FloorSat** for `--max-amount` (`:1887`, `:373-380`).
  - This bead defines the mode type and Millisat, and unit-tests Millisat. WholeSat, FloorSat and the whole-sat check are Phase 7a's helpers; reuse them. Phase 9a (2 of 2) applies WholeSat and FloorSat to fiat on the onchain commands.
  - Record in README, and in the golden allowlist, any difference from cyberkrill's `f64` results.
- **Fiat input grammar** (`parse_fiat_amount`, `main.rs:193-310`): a 3-letter alphabetic currency code after the number, in any case (a bitcoin unit is not a fiat code); no sign, leading dot or trailing dot; commas only in three-digit groups or Indian grouping. List under README "Deltas taken" any input the exact parser treats differently from cyberkrill's `f64` parse.
- **Output.** The stderr breadcrumb `[price-feed] median BTC/{currency} = {price:.2} from {n} feeds: {sources}` (`main.rs:334-347`), and `convert-amount`'s `fiat_source` object (`main.rs:1307-1322`).
- **Test URL override.** This bead owns the single test-only mechanism that points the app's HTTPS URLs at the localhost stub. Phase 9d reuses it, and so does Phase 9b for its fiat-amount price feeds, rather than adding their own. Phase 9b's LNURL URLs and Phase 9c's guardian URLs need none: they come from the address (`user@127.0.0.1:<port>`) and the invite. Default behaviour, with no override, uses cyberkrill's URLs.
  - The override is a parameter of the app's library entry points (base URLs for the feeds, CoinGecko and the DCA RPC URL), set only by the test driver in process. The CLI reads no override variable, so the release binary has none. Tests that spawn the binary pass explicit URL flags where the command has them (Phase 8a (2 of 2)'s connection rule).
  - This bead adds the in-process app entry point that takes the override and returns the exit code and the stderr text. Fiat and DCA tests use it (Phases 9a, 9b and 9d), since the spawn helper refuses those paths. The entry point takes the override as a required argument and refuses to run unless every URL in it names `127.0.0.1` and a port other than 8332. It applies the same two rules as Phase 8a (2 of 2)'s spawn-helper refusals (i) and (iv) to its own argv; they are restated here, so this bead does not depend on that one:
    - for `onchain-list-utxos`, `onchain-create-psbt`, `onchain-create-funded-psbt` and `onchain-move-utxos`, `--rpc-url` must be given and must name `127.0.0.1` and a port other than 8332; the default `http://127.0.0.1:8332` (`main.rs:11`) is refused;
    - no URL inside another argument (an invite, a Lightning address) may name port 8332.
    - Each refusal is tested, so an in-process test can never fall back to cyberkrill's default URLs.
  - In-process TLS tests set `SSL_CERT_FILE` to the test CA with `Std.Async.System.setEnvVar` before calling the entry point; spawned tests set it in the child's environment.
- **Fiat input arguments** (cyberkrill): `convert-amount` (`main.rs:632`) here. `create-psbt --outputs` (`:916`/`:1640`), `create-funded-psbt --outputs` (`:982`/`:1760`) and `move-utxos --max-amount` (`:1052`/`:1883`) are Phase 9a (2 of 2). `--fee` and `--fee-rate` take no fiat.

## Non-goals
- Fiat amounts on the onchain commands (Phase 9a, 2 of 2).
- `ln-generate-invoice` (Phase 9b), `fm-fetch-config` (Phase 9c).
- `onchain-dca-report`, which uses CoinGecko's history API rather than these feeds (Phase 9d).

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- Tests serve **a response fixture for every feed** on the localhost TLS stub, reached through `SSL_CERT_FILE` and the test URL override. No internet.
- **Fixtures are synthetic.** Provider bodies carry no licence, so none is committed. Each fixture is JSON we write ourselves in the provider's response shape, as defined by the fields cyberkrill's parser reads (`cyberkrill-core/src/price_feed.rs` @ `27cad1f`):
  - CoinGecko `bitcoin.<currency in lower case>` (`parse_coingecko_price` `:486`); Coinbase `data.rates.<CUR>` (`:496`); blockchain.info `<CUR>.last` (`:509`);
  - Kraken `error` (a non-empty array means no quote) and `result.<pair>.c[0]`, the only pair or else the first sorted pair ending in the currency (`:524`); Fedi `prices["BTC/USD"].rate` and `prices["<CUR>/USD"].rate` (`:570`, `fedi_pair_rate`); CEX.io `error` and `last` (`:607`);
  - Bitstamp `last` (`:623`); Yadio `error` and `rate` (`:634`); Gemini `result` (`"error"` means no quote) and `last` (`:649`).
  - Each fixture's sidecar says it is synthetic and cites the parser's file:line. The work session may fetch each URL once to confirm the shape, but commits no provider body. Error fixtures (404, error objects) are synthetic too. No API keys are involved; commit none.
  - Fixtures live under `packages/cyberkrill/test/http/`, inside the check derivation's source (`flake.nix:63`).
- **No golden against cyberkrill here.** cyberkrill's `reqwest` uses rustls with webpki-roots and ignores `SSL_CERT_FILE`, and its feed URLs are hardcoded `https://`, so it cannot be pointed at the stub. Expected JSON is derived from the fixtures plus the cited code, in one of two ways:
  - a committed script calls cyberkrill-core's parsing and aggregation functions from a throwaway clone at `27cad1f` on the fixtures, which also checks that each synthetic body has a shape cyberkrill parses; or
  - the values are derived by hand, and README marks them as hand-derived.
  - The throwaway-clone script follows AGENTS.md "Reference only": built inside that commit's own `nix develop` with dependencies fetched first, the test run offline inside `unshare -rn sh -c 'ip link set lo up && …'` with `HOME` set to a temp dir. description:

2. GET `https://{domain}/.well-known/lnurlp/{user}` (`:531-536`) and parse it as `LnurlPayRequest` (`:474`). Use `lightning`'s LUD-06/LUD-16 models.
3. Check `minSendable <= msats <= maxSendable` (`:539-547`), and the comment's length in bytes against `commentAllowed`, only when that field is present (`:550-558`).

Set explicit timeouts. cyberkrill uses `reqwest` with no timeout; list the difference in README's "Deltas taken".

Tests use the address `user@127.0.0.1:<stub port>`. Paying the invoice.

title: Phase 9c: fm-fetch-config (Fedimint federation config fetch over HTTPS)
description:
## Outcome
`fm-fetch-config <invite_code> [-o file]` (`main.rs:1968`; `fedimint-lite/src/lib.rs:453`; JSON `FederationConfigOutput` `lib.rs:437`) fetches a federation's config from its guardians over `http-curl` and matches cyberkrill on synthetic config responses served by the stub.

## Why this exists
This is a v1 HTTPS command (plan §4, Phase 9).

## Scope
As in `fedimint-lite/src/lib.rs` @ `27cad1f`:
- **Rewrite** each guardian URL: `wss://` → `https://` and `ws://` → `http://` (`:464-467`); trim every trailing `/` (`trim_end_matches('/')`, `:468`); request `{base}/config` (`:469`). The rewrite is a global `.replace` on the whole URL, not a prefix rewrite: every `wss://` and `ws://` in it is replaced.
- **Request:** GET first (`:499`). If the GET errors or is non-2xx, POST body `{}` with `Content-Type: application/json` (`:502-509`).
- **Guardians** are tried one at a time, and the first success wins (`:462`).
  - But `validate_federation_id(...)?` (`:474`) returns its error at once: a guardian whose config fails validation aborts the command without the next guardian being tried. So does an error from `parse_federation_config`, which `:476` returns directly: it rejects a `global.api_endpoints` that is not an object (`:593`), a peer-id key that is not a `u16` (`:597`) and a non-string endpoint URL (`:601`). A body that is not JSON is different: it fails inside `fetch_config_from_guardian` (`:521-524`), the loop's `Err` arm catches it (`:478-483`), and the next guardian is tried. Match all three.
- **Federation-id validation** (`:529-555`) is weak: it compares `config["federation_id"]` only when that field exists, and otherwise warns.
  - A config missing `global.api_endpoints` is a hard error (`:530-534`).
  - Match it. A stronger check would be a delta: it goes through the common follow-ups rule, not a silent change.
- **Parsing** follows `parse_federation_config` (`:557`).
- **Invite decode.** `fetch_fedimint_config` decodes the invite with `decode_fedimint_invite` (`:453-455`), so it goes through Phase 7c's app-side fallback exactly as `fm-decode-invite` does.
- **Timeouts.** cyberkrill uses `reqwest::Client::new()` with no timeout (`:457`). Set explicit timeouts, and list the difference in README's "Deltas taken".

## Non-goals
WebSocket support. The rewrite exists because the port speaks HTTPS only.

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- Tests replay **synthetic** config responses on the localhost stub. Never fetch or commit a live federation's config. Each body is JSON we write ourselves in the shape `parse_federation_config` (`fedimint-lite/src/lib.rs:557`) and `validate_federation_id` (`:529-555`) read: `global.api_endpoints` (required, `:530-534`), the optional `federation_id`, and whatever `parse_federation_config` copies into `FederationConfigOutput` (`:437`). Its sidecar says it is synthetic and cites those lines. The cases:
  - a GET success;
  - a GET failure followed by a POST success;
  - every guardian failing;
  - a federation-id mismatch;
  - a config without `global.api_endpoints`;
  - a non-JSON body (the next guardian is tried);
  - an `api_endpoints` array (abort).
- **Test invites** use `ws://` guardian URLs pointing at the plain-HTTP stub on `127.0.0.1`, which the rewrite turns into `http://`. Build them with Phase 6's encoder from a reviewed fedimint-lite vector, with only the URLs replaced; their provenance line names cyberkrill @ `27cad1f`, `fedimint-lite/src/lib.rs`, `MIT OR Apache-2.0` taken under MIT. No internet.
- **Goldens.** Because the stub is plain HTTP, cyberkrill can reach it. Capture inside `unshare -rn sh -c 'ip link set lo up && …'` (a new namespace's loopback starts down), with `HOME` set to a temp dir and the stub started in the same namespace.
- **Fixed port.** The test invites embed the stub URL (`ws://127.0.0.1:<port>`), so captures and the port's tests use the stub's fixed-port mode at one committed port. Captures run in their own `unshare -rn` namespace and the check sandbox in its own, so the port cannot collide there; on the host, a taken port stops the stub before its ready line (Phase 1b (2 of 2)), so the test fails instead of reaching another service.
- **Stub stdin.** The replay stub exits as soon as its stdin closes (Phase 1b (2 of 2), README "Replay server and command line"). A capture script that starts it in the background from a non-interactive shell hands it `/dev/null`, so it would stop at once. Start it with stdin held open, for example `sleep infinity | python3 -I packages/http-curl/test/responder.py --port <port> --log <log> <recordings> &`, wait for its `READY` line, and stop it by killing that pipeline after the capture.
- **Paths.** Canned responses live under `packages/cyberkrill/test/http/`, inside the check derivation's source (`flake.nix:63`).
- **Connection rule.** Port tests follow Phase 8a (2 of 2)'s connection rule: spawned cases go through its helper and the dev-shell `unshare` guard, or run in process. The helper's refusal (iv) covers this command's case, a URL inside an invite that names port 8332.

- Plan §4: Phase 9 depends on 1b, 5, 6 and 7. Here that means both Phase 1b beads, all three Phase 5 beads, Phase 6 and Phases 7a-7c.
- **As in the plan's table,** this bead also depends on Phase 8a (2 of 2), which owns the connection rule (spawn helper, dev-shell `unshare` guard, check-derivation marker) that this bead's spawned network tests use.
- Phase 10a (1 of 3) and Phase 10a (3 of 3) wait for this bead.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The `wss://`→`https://` rewrite is tested, including `ws://`, the trailing slash, and a URL with `ws://` past its start (the global replace).
- GET-then-POST fallback, guardian iteration and the id check are tested, including the abort on the first guardian whose config fails validation, the abort on the first guardian whose config `parse_federation_config` rejects, the move to the next guardian after a non-JSON body, and a URL ending in `//`.

title: Phase 9d: onchain-dca-report over Core RPC with CoinGecko historical prices
description:
## Outcome
`onchain-dca-report --descriptor <d> [--bitcoin-dir] [--currency usd] [--cache-dir] [-o]` (`main.rs:2585`; `cyberkrill-core/src/dca_report.rs:67`; JSON `DcaReport` `dca_report.rs:41`) works over Core RPC and gives the expected JSON derived from cyberkrill's code, on regtest RPC recordings and synthetic CoinGecko fixtures.

## Why this exists
This is a v1 network command (plan §1 scope; plan §4, Phase 9).

## Scope
As in `dca_report.rs` @ `27cad1f`:
- **RPC backend.** The URL is hardcoded to `http://127.0.0.1:8332` (`:170`), with no `--rpc-*` flags, and the bitcoin dir defaults to `$HOME/.bitcoin` (`main.rs:2597`).
  - Calls, in this order: `getblockchaininfo` (`bitcoin_rpc.rs:516`), then `scantxoutset` (`:178`, via `bitcoin_rpc.rs:534`, range 0..200), then `getrawtransaction` (`:194`) and **`getblock`** (`:204`) for each UTXO.
  - Phase 8a (1 of 2)'s generator already records `getblock` and this command's `scantxoutset` range.
  - Tests override the RPC URL through Phase 9a (1 of 2)'s test URL override. The default URL (`dca_report.rs:170`) matches cyberkrill and is tested only as a parsed value, never by connecting (Phase 8a (2 of 2)'s connection rule).
  - A `<0;1>` descriptor makes two `scantxoutset` calls (`bitcoin_rpc.rs:505-512`); a fixture that uses one needs both halves recorded.
- **Injectable "today".** The port takes today's date from a source that tests can set. It drives both the "current" price lookup (`dca_report.rs:368`) and the `report_date` field (`:139`, `Utc::now()`).
- **`backend` field.** cyberkrill prints `format!("{backend:?}")` (`:141`), for example `BitcoinCore { bitcoin_dir: "/path" }`, so the JSON embeds the `--bitcoin-dir` path (default `$HOME/.bitcoin`, `main.rs:2597`). Reproduce the Debug string exactly. DCA tests pass `--bitcoin-dir test/recordings/bitcoin-dir` (Phase 8a (1 of 2)'s committed throwaway cookie, relative to the package; DCA only reads it). The cookie then matches the recordings, and `backend` is the fixed `BitcoinCore { bitcoin_dir: "test/recordings/bitcoin-dir" }`, so no committed expected JSON holds a real or `/home/` path. One extra case passes `/nonexistent/bitcoin-dir`, where the unreadable cookie means no auth (`bitcoin_rpc.rs:390-405`), and asserts the 401 auth error. `HOME` is a temp dir.
- **Prices** come from CoinGecko history only, not the Phase 9a feeds: `https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/coins/bitcoin/history?date=DD-MM-YYYY` (`:444`).
  - The "current" price is today's history call (`:374`).
  - Calls are paced 300 ms apart (`:449`) with a 30-second timeout (`:427`).
  - The cache file is `{cache_dir}/btc_{cur}_{date}.json`, read at `:402-416` and written at `:499-516`.
  - **Errors.** A non-2xx CoinGecko reply returns no price (`:458-467`). For a UTXO's date that is only a warning, `No historical price found` (`:96-106`): the report continues, that UTXO's price stays null, and the exit status is 0. Only the **current** price's missing value fails the command (`:385-390`). A transport error or timeout (`:451-455`) and a JSON parse error (`:472-474`) exit non-zero.
- **Rejections.** The `--electrum` and `--esplora` backends are BDK and out of v1. Handle them as Phase 7a settled.
- Exact amounts. Any fiat arithmetic difference from cyberkrill's `f64` goes in README.

## Non-goals
BDK, Electrum and Esplora.

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- **Never run cyberkrill's `onchain-dca-report`.** It hardcodes `127.0.0.1:8332` and the `$HOME/.bitcoin` cookie, which is the owner's node.
  - Port tests set `HOME` to a temp dir, pass `--bitcoin-dir` at the committed cookie fixture (above), and override the RPC URL. They run in process through Phase 9a (1 of 2)'s entry point, since the spawn helper refuses `onchain-dca-report` (Phase 8a (2 of 2)'s connection rule). Nothing touches port 8332 or `~/.bitcoin`.
  - Any other run of cyberkrill happens inside `unshare -rn sh -c 'ip link set lo up && …'` (a new namespace's loopback starts down), with `HOME` set to a temp dir and any stub started inside.
- Regtest recordings only, from Phase 8a (1 of 2)'s generator. Never the owner's node.
  - If a test needs a request no recording holds, add a case to Phase 8a (1 of 2)'s case file and re-run the generator for the new case only (`--cases <new>`; regtest only, same safety rules; DCA cases use the generator's own client), committing its new recording file. Never hand-write one.
- **CoinGecko fixtures are synthetic.** Provider bodies carry no licence, so none is committed. Each history body is JSON we write ourselves in CoinGecko's response shape, as defined by the field cyberkrill reads: `market_data.current_price.<currency in lower case>` (`dca_report.rs:483-487`). Its sidecar says it is synthetic and cites that line. The work session may fetch one history URL once to confirm the shape, but commits no provider body. Error replies are synthetic too. No internet in tests.
  - The UTXO dates are those in Phase 8a (1 of 2)'s DCA recordings, whose mocktime that bead picked. Build the bodies for exactly those dates, plus the injected "today".
  - Fixtures live under `packages/cyberkrill/test/http/`, inside the check derivation's source (`flake.nix:63`).
- **No golden against cyberkrill.** Expected JSON is derived from the recordings and fixtures plus the cited code, as in Phase 9a: a committed script over cyberkrill-core in a throwaway clone, or by hand, marked in README.
  - The throwaway-clone script follows AGENTS.md "Reference only" (that commit's own `nix develop`, dependencies fetched first, the test run offline inside `unshare -rn sh -c 'ip link set lo up && …'` with `HOME` set to a temp dir). It calls only the pure `calculate_dca_metrics` (`dca_report.rs:535`; private, so the temporary `#[test]` goes in that file's own `mod tests`, `dca_report.rs:595`). Never `generate_dca_report` (`:67`) or any `fetch_*`: `fetch_utxos_bitcoind` builds its client on `http://127.0.0.1:8332` with the caller's cookie (`:160-175`), and the price lookups reach `api.coingecko.com` (`:367-374`, `:444`).
- The cache dir is written only where the user points it. Tests use a temp dir.

### Common definition of done (plan §4, every work session)
- `nix build` and `nix flake check` exit 0. The flake check runs `lake build && lake test` for every package listed in `lakePackages` in `flake.nix`, inside the nix sandbox, then runs the app. Stage new files (`git add`) before running `nix flake check`: a flake sees only tracked files.
- In each touched package, `nix develop -c lake build` and `nix develop -c lake test` exit 0.
- No `sorry`: `grep -rnw sorry --include='*.lean' --exclude-dir=.lake packages` prints nothing (CI runs the same check from Phase 2 on).
- `#print axioms` on every theorem this bead lists shows only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. Each listed theorem is added to the package's committed axiom-gate test (Phase 2's pattern); `lake test` fails on any axiom outside the three. The gate is an allowlist of those three and contains no "sorry" substring. No `native_decide` in library or proof modules; test files may use it.
- The vector counts this bead states pass. Each test asserts that the number of vectors it loaded equals a pinned constant, so a dropped vector fails, and the test output prints each count (for example `<set> valid: N/N`).
- `README.md` is updated: what the package now provides, vector sources and counts, and anything this bead says to document.
- `AGENTS.md` rules hold, including "Reference only" for any value taken from cyberkrill. New Lean, C and script files we write carry the dual-licence header; third-party and copied files follow the rule below, and JSON and other formats without comments need none.
- **Safety.** Tests use only published vectors, published test mnemonics, the BOLT #11 specification's published example private key (tests only), recordings from a throwaway regtest node, and synthetic or script-generated fixtures under the third-party rule (for example cyberkrill's captured outputs on those inputs, synthetic provider responses, our own LNURL and LUD JSON, values a committed script derives from published inputs). Never anything from the owner's node, wallets or devices. Tests never reach the internet, port 8332 or `~/.bitcoin`. Nothing committed contains private keys, seeds, xprvs, tprvs or WIF keys, or real addresses, xpubs or device dumps, apart from that BOLT #11 example key. No hardware wallets, no signing outside test vectors, no broadcast, no mainnet funds.
- **Third-party material** (`AGENTS.md` "Licence", plan §5):
  - Admitted in the tree, each with a provenance sidecar or header line (source URL, commit, path, licence), never the dual-licence header: MIT, BSD, ISC, CC0 or public domain, and CC-BY-4.0 (attribution and a note of any changes, for example "extracted and reformatted", kept in the sidecar). Material offered under a choice that includes MIT (such as fedimint-lite's `MIT OR Apache-2.0`) is taken under MIT.
  - Kept out of the tree: Apache-2.0-only, share-alike (CC-BY-SA) and unlicensed material. Use a pinned non-flake input read at test time, or replace it with vectors we generate ourselves.
  - Copied code whose upstream file has no header gets a provenance comment (upstream repo, commit, path, "MIT") with the upstream MIT notice in a file beside it, never the dual-licence header.
  - In a Lean file the provenance line is the first line and a `--` line comment (or `/- … -/`), never a `/-! … -/` doc comment, for example `-- Copied from <repo> @ <commit>, <path>; MIT, see <notice file>`. JSON and other formats without comments get the sidecar.
- **Stop mechanics.** If this bead says stop and report: commit no weakened statement, `br defer` the bead, add label `owner-decision`, comment what was tried (`br comments add`), and end the work session blocked.
- **Follow-ups.** A delta or stricter check you think v1 needs goes in a new bead created deferred with label `owner-decision`, and in README "Deltas not taken". Never implement it unranked.
- **Upstream fixes.** A fix that would also help upstream (lean4-hash, lean-miniscript) goes in the committed `docs/upstream-fixes.md` (file, problem, fix), not in a br comment. Phase 10a (3 of 3) turns that file into patches.
